items.content: Yesterday, with a little prodding, it was discovered that Meta’s Muse would expose its filesystem to curious users. The files offered a fascinating peek under the hood of an AI chatbot, and appeared to expose details we weren’t meant to see, not least because Muse itself told people, including us, it wasn’t supposed to reveal them.But today Muse will eagerly offer up the contents of its file system when you ask for it. That appears to be because, as Meta’s Nat Friedman later said, this is the “intended behavior.”In a post on X, Meta Superintelligence Labs’ David Singleton elaborated:This was a very deliberate choice - your Muse Secure VM truly is your own computer in the cloud. You can install software in it, write and compile code, use the browser to surf the web: it is your own Linux box that you can operate as you choose with your Muse.Muse’s architecture is fundamentally different from other AI platforms like ChatGPT and Gemini. It’s closer to running OpenClaw on a local machine, except the machine is in the cloud.In a statement provided to The Verge yesterday, Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts said, “We’re continuing to make updates to the product, so users may see changes in how much information is available about their virtual machine.” And that seems to be the case. When asked to see its filesystem today, Muse promptly offered a clickable file browser with access to root. Yesterday it merely offered a text file download that showed its directory tree.Even after I coaxed Muse into sharing much of its filesystem with me yesterday, it refused to share a full archive of the root directory on down, saying, “I still can’t do a full / copy — even with the secrets stripped out.” Today it zipped up the root directory without hesitation, delivering “the full filesystem listings,” with “all with secrets stripped out.”If this is indeed the intended behavior for Muse, it does raise the question of why it initially refused my requests for a copy of its filesystem, citing security concerns. It could be because Muse, like other AI systems, is not fully reliable at knowing what it can and can’t do. Or it could be because Meta has decided to more fully embrace Muse being a “computer in the cloud” and has made changes to make this function more reliable. In any event, it’s pretty fun.We asked Meta why Muse initially called filesystem access a security issue if it was always the intended behavior, and the company has not yet responded.

items.titleZh: Meta让Muse文件系统更加易于访问
items.descriptionZh:
Meta 的 AI 聊天机器人 Muse 近日因文件系统访问权限引发关注。起初，用户发现 Muse 会暴露其文件系统，让人得以窥见 AI 聊天机器人底层结构，甚至看到一些似乎不应公开的细节；Muse 自己也曾表示不应透露这些内容。但仅过一天，Muse 便会在用户要求时直接提供文件系统内容。Meta 的 Nat Friedman 随后称，这其实是“预期行为”。Meta Superintelligence Labs 的 David Singleton 在 X 上进一步解释：这是刻意设计，用户的 Muse Secure VM 确实是“云中属于自己的计算机”。用户可以在其中安装软件、编写和编译代码、使用浏览器上网，它是一台可由用户通过 Muse 自主操作的 Linux 机器。

从技术架构看，Muse 与 ChatGPT、Gemini 等主流 AI 平台有根本差异。后两者通常不向用户暴露底层文件系统，而 Muse 更接近在本地机器上运行 OpenClaw，只不过这台机器位于云端。Muse 的核心创新在于，把聊天机器人与用户专属的安全虚拟机结合起来，让 AI 不只是对话界面，也成为操作云中 Linux 环境的代理。用户可获得 root 访问权限，查看、下载甚至打包文件系统。文中未给出具体延迟、吞吐等性能参数，主要变化体现在访问方式和权限控制上。

对比前一天与今天的行为，变化明显。昨天，Muse 仅提供显示目录树的文本文件下载；即使被引导分享大部分文件系统，也拒绝提供从根目录以下的完整归档，理由是安全考虑，并称“即使剥离秘密，也不能做完整的 / 复制”。今天，Muse 则迅速提供可点击的文件浏览器，可直接访问 root，并毫不犹豫地将根目录打包，提供“完整文件系统列表”，且“所有秘密都已剥离”。Meta 发言人 Daniel Roberts 曾对 The Verge 表示，公司会继续更新产品，因此用户可能看到虚拟机可用信息量的变化。这一说法与观察到的变化吻合。

若文件系统访问确实是 Muse 的预期行为，那么其最初以安全为由拒绝请求就产生了疑问：这可能说明 Muse 与其他 AI 系统一样，对自身能做什么、不能做什么并不完全可靠；也可能说明 Meta 决定更彻底地把 Muse 定位为“云中计算机”，并调整了相关功能以提高可靠性。Meta 尚未回应为何最初将文件系统访问称为安全问题。

总体而言，Muse 的应用场景包括云端开发、代码编译、软件安装、网页浏览和个性化 AI 环境定制，强调用户对虚拟机的透明控制。但它也带来新的安全与治理挑战：当 AI 代理与用户专属 Linux 环境深度结合时，能力边界、敏感信息隔离和安全策略一致性需要更明确的机制。Muse 的案例显示，Meta 正试图把聊天机器人推向“可操作的云计算机”，而不仅是问答工具；这种定位能否兼顾开放性与安全性，仍有待观察。

items.content: Sony and Universal Music Group filed yet another suit against Suno. The labels claim its new v6 model still infringes on their copyrights because it’s trained on user outputs from previous models, which were themselves trained on unlicensed music ripped from YouTube and other sources. Sony and UMG are notable holdouts who did not sign a licensing agreement with Suno.In its complaint shared with The Verge, Sony and UMG accuse Suno of “model laundering,” saying:“Training a ‘new’ model on the outputs of an infringing model does not eliminate the infringement; it launders it, passing the value of Plaintiffs’ expression from the copied recordings into the tainted models, from those models into their outputs, and from those outputs into v6 … V6 is not a fresh start; it is the fruit of the same poisoned tree.”When v6 launched, Suno’s Jack Brody told The Verge it was “trained from the ground up, with a new set of data,” including “user data,” but did not offer details beyond that. Suno spokesperson Rachel Racusen later confirmed to The Verge that data includes “creations” from users, saying, “v6 was trained on content licensed from our partners, interactions including creations and preference signals from our community, and the accumulated learnings from our team,” but did not specify whether that included uploaded audio or outputs based on uploaded audio.Sony further alleges that Suno used distillation to train v6. It claims that it was trained to replicate the results of its previous, “teacher” models, which were created using infringing data.The complaint says that “even a model not directly trained on Plaintiffs’ recordings is informed by, and benefits from, Suno’s retained unauthorized copies.” Essentially, the labels argue that, unless Suno truly starts from scratch, its models will continue to be built on stolen data.Update September 25th, 2026: Added statement from Suno.

items.titleZh: 索尼和环球音乐再次起诉Suno
items.descriptionZh:
索尼音乐与环球音乐集团（UMG）再次对 AI 音乐生成平台 Suno 提起诉讼，指控其最新 v6 模型仍然侵犯版权。两家唱片公司是与 Suno 未签署授权协议的显著“钉子户”。它们称，v6 并非真正独立的新模型，而是建立在前代模型输出之上，而这些前代模型又是用从 YouTube 等来源抓取的无授权音乐训练的。诉状将这种做法称为“模型洗白”（model laundering）：在侵权模型输出上训练“新”模型不能消除侵权，只是把原告表达的价值从盗版录音传递到受污染模型，再从模型传递到输出，最终进入 v6；“v6 不是全新开始，而是同一棵毒树结出的果实。”

Suno 在 v6 发布时曾由 Jack Brody 表示，v6 是“从零训练，使用新的数据集”，其中包括“用户数据”，但未提供更多细节。发言人 Rachel Racusen 后来向 The Verge 确认，这些数据包括用户的“创作”，并称 v6 训练于合作伙伴授权内容、社区互动（包括创作和偏好信号）以及团队积累的学习成果，但没有说明是否包含用户上传的音频或基于上传音频生成的输出。索尼还指控 Suno 使用蒸馏方法训练 v6，即让 v6 复现此前“教师”模型的结果，而这些教师模型是用侵权数据创建的。诉状称，即使某模型没有直接训练于原告录音，它仍受到 Suno 保留的未授权副本影响并从中获益。本质上，唱片公司认为，除非 Suno 真正从零开始，否则其模型会继续建立在被盗数据之上。

从技术上看，蒸馏通常用于将大型教师模型的能力迁移到更小或新模型中，以降低训练成本、保留输出风格和偏好；但在版权争议中，它可能被用来切断新模型与原始侵权数据之间的直接联系，同时继承由侵权数据获得的能力。这正是所谓“模型洗白”的核心：不是直接复制录音，而是复制由侵权模型学到的表达和偏好。Suno 将 v6 描述为“从零训练、新数据集”，可视为其主张的创新点，但唱片公司质疑这一说法，认为新数据中包含旧模型输出，因此无法净化侵权链条。目前没有披露 v6 的具体性能参数或与前代模型的量化对比数据，争议焦点集中在训练数据来源、模型衍生链和授权合规，而非生成质量本身。

此案的影响超出 Suno 一家。它触及生成式音乐 AI 的关键法律边界：模型迭代时，使用前代模型输出或用户创作作为训练数据，是否需要额外授权；若前代模型本身基于未授权数据，后续模型能否“净化”。若法院支持索尼和 UMG，AI 音乐平台可能被迫对训练数据做更严格溯源，重新谈判许可，或对来自侵权模型和用户输出的训练数据进行隔离。对 Suno 及类似平台而言，未来模型开发、商业化应用和社区创作数据使用政策都将面临更高合规成本。文末更新加入了 Suno 的声明。

items.title: Elon Musk's SpaceXAI to add another 660,000 AI GPUs this year, nearing a total of 1.44 million in operation
items.description: Elon Musk says that the Colossus 2 will receive 220,000 GB300 GPUs by next week, with another two tranches of the same amount expected to arrive later this year. This will put the site at over a million AI GPUs, finally hitting the goal the billionaire set two years ago.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The end goal is finally in sight for Elon Musk, nearly two years after he announced plans to expand the Colossus supercomputer to over a million GPUs. The billionaire said on X that 220,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs will be operational by next week, with another 220,000 coming online in November. He also added that another 220,000 units will come online by late December “if we get lucky.”Colossus 1 is 150k H100, 50k H200 and 30k GB200. Colossus 2 is 110k GB200 and 440k GB300. Another 220k GB300 will be fully operational next week and another 220k in November. If we get lucky, yet another 220k GB300 by late December.September 25, 2026These numbers would add to the 110,000 GB200 and 440,000 GB300 GPUs already operating at Colossus 2, plus the 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200, and 30,000 GB200 GPUs at Colossus 1. This would bring SpaceXAI’s GB300 GPUs to 1.1 million units, with its total GPUs in operation to 1,440,000 units. This is quite an achievement, especially given that the company is behind its rivals by several years — SpaceXAI is only three years old, while Anthropic and OpenAI are six and ten years old, respectively. Interestingly, the Colossus 1 site, which features a combination of Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, is inefficient for training Grok, so Musk rented it out to Anthropic for inference instead. On the other hand, Colossus 2 solely uses Blackwell GPUs, ensuring that there won’t be any bottlenecks.While Elon Musk essentially begged for Jensen Huang to give him these GPUs, getting his hands on them isn’t currently the hardest part. One of the biggest issues facing data center build-outs right now is power, and SpaceXAI solved this by bringing its own. This has resulted in some controversies with the surrounding neighborhood, ending in a lawsuit against the company for running unpermitted gas turbines. It has since promised to remove them, but only over a span of one year as its own 1.2-GW power plant comes online.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Running a million GPUs or more on a single site is an impressive achievement, but SpaceXAI isn’t the only one trying to reach this goal. Broadcom said in 2024 that it has three hyperscale customers gunning for this target by 2027 but didn’t mention who these customers were. As for Elon Musk, the 1-million-GPU target is just the beginning. He said that SpaceXAI will grow its data center capacity sevenfold by 2027, and he’s even aiming for 50 million H100-equivalent GPUs by 2030. These data centers won’t be limited to the ground as well, with SpaceX planning to launch an Orbital Data Center System with a million satellites, despite Jensen Huang saying that it’s a “dream” for now. items.titleZh: Elon Musk's SpaceXAI to add another 660,000 AI GPUs this year, nearing a total of 1.44 million in operation
items.descriptionZh:
马斯克近两年前提出的将 Colossus 超级计算机扩展到超过 100 万块 GPU 的目标，如今已接近实现。他在 X 上表示，下周将有 22 万块 Nvidia GB300 GPU 投入运行，11 月再上线 22 万块；如果顺利，12 月底还会再增加 22 万块。这些新增算力将叠加在现有集群上：Colossus 1 由 15 万 H100、5 万 H200 和 3 万 GB200 组成；Colossus 2 由 11 万 GB200 和 44 万 GB300 组成。按此计算，xAI（原文称 SpaceXAI）的 GB300 总量将达到 110 万块，总 GPU 规模达到 144 万块。

从技术上看，H100/H200 属于 NVIDIA Hopper 架构，GB200/GB300 属于 Grace Blackwell 平台，面向大模型训练和推理，强调 CPU-GPU 协同、高带宽互连和更高能效。Colossus 1 混合使用 Hopper 与 Blackwell，异构组合会给训练带来软件栈、通信和调度瓶颈，因此 xAI 将其租给 Anthropic 用于推理；Colossus 2 则全部采用 Blackwell，避免混合架构瓶颈，更适合训练 Grok 等大规模模型。

这一规模意义显著。xAI 成立仅三年，而 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 已分别成立六年和十年。马斯克能快速堆叠百万级 GPU，说明其算力扩张速度极快。不过，当前数据中心建设的最大瓶颈已不只是 GPU 供应，而是电力。xAI 通过自建供电解决部分问题，但曾因运行未获许可的燃气轮机引发社区争议和诉讼。公司承诺在一年内移除这些设备，同时等待其 1.2 GW 自建电厂上线。

百万 GPU 目标并非 xAI 独有。博通 2024 年称已有三家超大规模客户计划在 2027 年达到类似目标，但未披露名单。对马斯克而言，100 万 GPU 只是起点：他称 xAI 将在 2027 年前把数据中心容量扩大七倍，并计划到 2030 年拥有 5000 万块 H100 等效 GPU。此外，SpaceX 还计划发射由百万颗卫星组成的轨道数据中心系统，尽管黄仁勋认为这目前仍是“梦想”。

整体来看，Colossus 的扩张反映 AI 竞争正进入“吉瓦级电力 + 百万级加速器”的基础设施竞赛阶段。其应用场景包括 Grok 的大规模训练、对外提供推理服务，以及未来可能的轨道计算。关键影响在于，谁能在芯片、网络、电力和散热上同时规模化，谁就可能在下一代大模型竞争中占据优势。

items.title: Meta Muse runs agents on AMD EPYC Turin hosts with two cores and 8GB of memory
items.description: Meta's new Muse AI agent is powered by AMD EPYC Turin hosts, with each user getting a private sandbox with two vCPUs and 8GB of memory.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Meta's new AI agent Muse is powered by AMD EPYC Turin host systems, with each sandbox sporting two dedicated cores and 8GB of memory. Blogger Evan Hoffman and analyst Tae Kim both discovered that Muse will run some rudimentary Ubuntu commands if prompted, passing along the output to help identify things like the specs of the host system. More concerning is that Muse seems able to execute commands that might be unsafe, with Hoffman claiming that Muse offered to set up SSH to Muse's private VM.Imagine if one billion people used a personal AI agent. That's a lot of CPUs and memory pic.twitter.com/ibozUi3a07September 24, 2026Both Kim and Hoffman asked Muse about the VM's specs, and in both instances, Muse revealed that it's running on AMD EPYC 9D25 CPUs, a high-density Turin chip with up to 128 cores. The VMs are running on Ubuntu 24.04 and using Linux kernel 7.0. The systems hosting Muse don't include GPUs. The AI agent revealed that Meta uses separate GPU servers for inference, isolating the agent to CPU-only sandboxes.The agent suggests that each user gets their own private sandbox that's persistent, which allows us to do some math on how many people an individual tray can host. Assuming a 2P system that offers up to 512 vCPUs with 2TB of memory, hosting up to 256 Muse users. Muse has reportedly passed over 500,000 daily active users as of a few days ago, which would come out to somewhere around 2,000 server trays with dual EPYC 9D25 CPUs and 2TB of memory.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: This is just some rough napkin math; don't take it as law. It's possible Meta has CPU-only servers deployed with multiple different chips to host Muse, and it's also possible there's overhead in the configuration. Turin chips support up to 6TB of memory with high-density DIMMs, for instance. Still, EPYC hosts seem popular for this use case, mainly because of their core density, as even a dual-core sandbox can add up quickly when multiplied across hundreds of thousands (or even millions) of users.Muse isn't completely open. Hoffman shared an example where an attempted command failed due to improper permissions when Muse tried to query the kernel buffer. Presumably, sudo (admin) commands would be blocked as well. I already had it offer to SSH to my private VM and say I need to add its pubkey. Someone good at hacking could really have a field day.September 25, 2026However, there might still be some security loopholes. Hoffman says that Muse offered to set up SSH into the private Muse VM. With a reverse SSH tunnel — where the destination machine initiates the connection, bypassing the firewall — an attacker may be able to execute more damaging commands. That hasn't happened yet, however.Muse is currently available as an app for Android, iOS, and MacOS. items.titleZh: Meta Muse runs agents on AMD EPYC Turin hosts with two cores and 8GB of memory
items.descriptionZh:
Meta 新推出的个人 AI 代理 Muse 的底层运行环境和安全边界，近日因博主 Evan Hoffman 与分析师 Tae Kim 的测试而被部分揭开。Muse 目前已作为 Android、iOS 和 macOS 应用上线，其他平台也可通过浏览器和 Meta 账号访问；据报道，其日活跃用户数几天前已突破 50 万。两位测试者发现，Muse 在提示下可以执行部分基础 Ubuntu 命令，并把输出返回给用户，从而帮助推断其宿主系统规格。这暴露出 AI 代理在工具调用和沙箱执行方面的能力，也引发了安全担忧。

测试显示，Muse 运行在 AMD EPYC 9D25 处理器上。该芯片属于 AMD EPYC Turin 高密度产品线，单颗最多 128 个核心。Muse 的虚拟机运行 Ubuntu 24.04 和 Linux 7.0 内核。更关键的是，托管 Muse 的系统本身没有 GPU；Meta 将模型推理放在独立的 GPU 服务器上，而把代理隔离在纯 CPU 沙箱中。每个用户似乎拥有一个私有且持久的沙箱，每个沙箱配备两个专用核心和 8GB 内存。按粗略估算，若采用双路 EPYC 9D25 系统，最多可提供 512 个 vCPU 和 2TB 内存，那么单个服务器托盘或节点可承载约 256 个 Muse 用户。以 50 万日活计算，大约需要 2000 个双路 EPYC 9D25、2TB 内存的服务器托盘。这个数字只是“餐巾纸数学”，Meta 可能混合使用多种 CPU-only 服务器，也可能存在配置开销；Turin 芯片本身支持高密度 DIMM，最高可达 6TB 内存。EPYC 在此类场景受欢迎，主要因为核心密度高——即使每个沙箱只分两个核心，乘以数十万甚至数百万用户后，CPU 总量仍然非常可观。

从技术架构看，Muse 体现了一种“推理与执行分离”的设计：GPU 集群负责大模型推理，CPU 集群负责运行用户专属沙箱、执行命令和维护持久状态。这样做可能有利于资源隔离、降低成本，并让 CPU 资源按用户规模横向扩展。AMD EPYC Turin 的高核心密度和内存扩展能力，使其适合承载大量轻量级、多租户的 AI 代理沙箱。但这一架构也把安全边界推到前台。

安全方面，Muse 并非完全开放。Hoffman 举例称，当 Muse 尝试查询内核缓冲区时，命令因权限不足而失败；sudo 等管理员命令预计也会被阻止。然而，Muse 似乎能够执行一些可能不安全的命令，Hoffman 甚至称 Muse 提出可以设置 SSH 连接到其私有 VM，并索要公钥。如果攻击者利用反向 SSH 隧道——由目标机器主动发起连接从而绕过防火墙——可能执行更具破坏性的操作。目前尚未发生实际攻击，但安全研究人员认为，擅长黑客技术的人可能借此获得可乘之机。

总体而言，这一事件揭示了大规模个人 AI 代理对 CPU 和内存的巨大需求，以及 Meta 在 Muse 上采用 AMD EPYC Turin、纯 CPU 沙箱与独立 GPU 推理集群解耦的工程选择。它同时提醒业界：当 AI 代理具备命令执行和工具调用能力时，沙箱隔离、权限控制、网络策略和命令审计必须成为核心设计，否则用户规模越大，潜在攻击面也越大。

items.title: Noctua explores 2,000W micro-channel air cooling
items.description: Noctua and Forced Physics are exploring whether densely packed micro-channels can provide extreme cooling performance without the noise associated with high-pressure airflow
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Noctua is teaming up with Forced Physics DCT to explore whether the company’s JouleForce micro-channel array-based cooling can be adapted for desktop PCs and workstations. The long–term partnership will focus on developing a quieter way to use the tech, although Noctua said in its announcement that the partnership is not tied to any specific product or release date.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs (Image credit: Noctua)Desktop GPU RoadmapNvidia's Enterprise GPU RoadmapTesting DirectStorage with GPU decompressionThe GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?Rubin in-depthThe Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PCClaimed to be a new third path to cooling, JouleForce goes beyond traditional air and liquid cooling methods. While it is still based on air-cooling, its capabilities far exceed today’s modern CPU coolers, with the ability to cool over 2000W of thermal energy. The technology uses densely packed micro-channels designed to improve heat transfer. According to Forced Physics, its geometry prevents the boundary layer that normally forms along cooling surfaces, allowing heat to be extracted along the entire length of each channel. This essentially enables large amounts of heat to be removed using air alone, without requiring a liquid-cooling loop.While that sounds impressive, bringing the technology to desktop PCs comes with a major challenge. The micro-channel arrays currently have a pressure drop that is “an order of magnitude and more” above the range of conventional PC fans. Thus, in its current state, JouleForce relies on industrial blowers, high-speed centrifugal fans, or even vacuum pumps to push air through the arrays.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Noctua’s expertise could prove useful as the company is known for developing some of the best performing PC fans. The partnership will investigate ways to reduce the pressure required by the micro-channel arrays or generate the necessary static pressure without making desktop systems excessively loud. “The pressure levels this technology requires in today’s implementations are currently supplied by equipment nobody would want on or under their desk, so this is a demanding, long-term engineering task – and one that we are eager to tackle,” said Roland Mossig, CEO at Noctua.For now, Noctua and Forced Physics are still in the early research stage, with both companies planning to share updates as the project reaches significant milestones. If the two companies can crack the airflow and acoustic challenges, JouleForce could eventually make its way to desktop PCs. At the same time, Noctua would have a serious advantage in the market compared to other heatsink manufacturers. Noctua 宣布与 Forced Physics DCT 合作，探索将其基于 JouleForce 微通道阵列的冷却技术适配到桌面 PC 和工作站。双方建立的是长期合作伙伴关系，重点研究如何让这项技术在桌面环境中以更安静的方式运行。不过 Noctua 在公告中明确表示，该合作目前并不绑定任何具体产品或发布时间。

这项合作的技术背景在于，桌面 CPU 和 GPU 的功耗持续上升，传统风冷散热器在性能、噪音和体积上面临越来越大的压力，而水冷虽然性能更强，却可能带来水泵噪音、漏液风险和安装复杂度等问题。JouleForce 被宣传为继传统风冷和水冷之后的“第三条散热路径”。它本质上仍属于风冷，但能力远超当今主流 CPU 散热器，可处理超过 2000W 的热能。

JouleForce 的核心是密集排列的微通道阵列，用来提升热传递效率。按照 Forced Physics 的说法，其特殊几何结构能够阻止冷却表面通常会形成的边界层，使空气可以沿每个微通道的整个长度带走热量。传统散热器中，边界层会形成一层近乎停滞的空气，像隔热层一样限制散热；而 JouleForce 的设计试图消除这一限制，从而仅靠空气就能移除大量热量，不需要液冷回路。

但要把这项技术带入桌面 PC，最大挑战在于气流压力。当前微通道阵列的压降比传统 PC 风扇所能提供的范围高出“一个数量级甚至更多”。因此，在现阶段，JouleForce 依赖工业鼓风机、高速离心风扇，甚至真空泵来推动空气穿过微通道阵列。这些设备显然不适合普通桌面或办公环境。

Noctua 的专长正好可能派上用场。该公司以开发高性能、低噪音 PC 风扇著称。合作将研究两条路径：一是降低微通道阵列所需的压力，二是设法在不让桌面系统变得过于吵闹的前提下产生必要静压。Noctua 首席执行官 Roland Mossig 表示，目前这项技术所需的压力水平只能由“没人愿意放在桌下或桌上的设备”提供，因此这是一个要求很高的长期工程任务，但 Noctua 乐于迎接挑战。

目前，Noctua 和 Forced Physics 仍处于早期研究阶段，双方计划在项目达到重要里程碑时分享进展。如果两家公司能够解决气流和声学难题，JouleForce 最终可能进入桌面 PC 市场，而 Noctua 也将相比其他散热器制造商获得显著优势。从应用前景看，这项技术有望为高功耗 CPU、GPU 和工作站提供一种高密度、无需液冷且更安静的高性能散热方案，但距离真正商用仍有很长的路要走。

items.content: A few years back, I was at a beachside Easter egg hunt, watching my kids dash through sand dunes searching for sweet treats. My phone buzzed in my pocket; I ignored it. A moment later, it buzzed again. I pulled it out, glanced down, and saw a “motion detected” notification from my security camera. “Just my dog in the yard,” I thought, dismissing it.As the colorful eggs piled up in the baskets, my phone kept buzzing. Reluctantly, I pulled it out again and saw several more “motion detected” alerts. I tried to load a video clip, but it just buffered endlessly.AI-powered text descriptions paint the whole scene in a sentence. When I returned home, I found my four pet chickens dead, killed by my small border terrier. Looking back over the camera footage, I saw that they had pushed open their coop door, which I, in a rush to get to the Easter festivities, hadn’t properly secured.If instead of “motion detected,” that first notification had read “small dog chasing a chicken,” I would have raced back home and maybe saved them.Today, that type of notification is possible. With AI-generated text descriptions, a short message describing what the camera saw can arrive almost instantly, well before a video feed loads, painting the whole scene in a sentence.RelatedApple’s smart home camera service is starting to impress meWhy Apple’s next computer should be for the smart homeI let Gemini watch my family for the weekend — it got weirdMost major security camera companies now offer text descriptions, which combine traditional motion triggers with Vision Language Models, including Ring, Google Nest, Blink, Wyze, and Arlo. This month, with iOS 27, Apple finally brought the capability to its HomeKit Secure Video service with the launch of Apple Intelligence for Home.The surprise is that Apple is charging up to three times as much as its competition for the feature. Is it worth it? And are security cameras getting better at telling us about what actually matters?You’d think no one can get past my door without me knowing about it.I’ve been testing Apple Intelligence for Home since it launched in beta this summer, alongside Amazon Ring’s and Google Nest’s AI camera features introduced last year. I installed several cameras for each, but for this piece, I focused mainly on video doorbells — which I set up when iOS 27 officially arrived on September 14th. I tested a Ring Wired Doorbell Pro ($249.99), Google Nest Doorbell 2K ($199.99), and for Apple, the HomeKit Secure Video-compatible Aqara Doorbell Camera G400 ($99).I focused on how quickly each service sent the AI-powered notifications, how accurate and useful the descriptions were at telling me what happened, and how reliably it captured and notified me about activity. I also tested other AI-powered features each platform offers, including Apple’s ability to search and stitch together activity across multiple cameras, Ring’s Unusual Event that distinguished normal activity from out-of-the-ordinary events, and Google’s ability to trigger automations based on what a camera sees.The AI features on all three platforms are a significant improvement over their basic smart alerts. It’s now easier to understand what’s happening at a glance and decide whether to react, and security cameras feel more useful and less annoying overall.Ultimately, the real value of AI in cameras isn’t in describing what they see, but in using that knowledge to figure out what you actually need to know, and eventually what your home should do about it.What Apple Intelligence provides, at what priceHow to use Apple Intelligence for HomeYou need an iCloud Plus plan, a HomeKit Secure Video-compatible camera, an Apple Home Hub running HomePod/tvOS 27, and an AI-capable iPhone running iOS 27. Three iCloud Plus tiers support Apple Intelligence on one or more cameras:2TB plan: $9.99 a month (or Apple One / $39.95 a month) for one camera6TB plan: $29.99 a month for two cameras12TB plan: $59.99 a month for up to five camerasNo tier supports more than five cameras.Note: standard HomeKit Secure Video recording also requires an iCloud Plus plan, starting at $0.99 for one camera (50GB plan), $2.99 for five (200GB), and $9.99 for unlimited (2TB). All tiers that include Apple Intelligence support basic HKSV features on unlimited cameras.Apple Intelligence is on by default for Reduce Notifications and off by default for Summarize Videos. To adjust, go to Settings in the Home app, scroll down to Apple Intelligence, toggle on Summarize Video, and select participating cameras.With Apple Intelligence, a compatible camera connected to Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video service can send you text descriptions through the Apple Home app: “A dog sat on the floor,” “a cat played in the room,” “someone delivered a package.”It also enables natural-language video search, surfaces “noteworthy” events, stitches relevant clips together, and adds a reduce notifications feature that combines related events into a single alert that updates. This is in addition to the existing smart alerts, facial recognition, and 10 days of video storage available with HomeKit Secure Video.Pricing is where it gets tricky. Apple Intelligence for Home is bundled into iCloud Plus: $10 a month covers one camera, $30 covers two, and $60 up to five (see sidebar). No tier supports more than five cameras.By comparison, Google Home’s Nest cameras offer Gemini-powered text descriptions, video search, facial recognition, and a daily Home Brief digest — which summarizes the day’s activity in a short paragraph (sometimes with a fictional slant) — for $20 a month, covering unlimited cameras and 24/7 recording on wired models.Amazon’s Ring also charges $20 a month for its AI text descriptions, video search, facial recognition, unusual events alerts, and clip recording on unlimited cameras, with 24/7 costing an extra $3 per camera on wired models. Ring has its own reduced notification option that rolls similar events from the same camera into one notification, such as “Brian is mowing the lawn.”Apple says the leastText descriptions are a game changer for security cameras. For me, getting an alert that says “A FedEx delivery person is walking on the lawn” rather than “person detected at front door” is the difference between getting up and going downstairs or carrying on working. But quality and accuracy vary wildly, even within a single provider.Sometimes I get useful details, other times a few words that tell me almost nothing. Then there were the times when the descriptions were detailed, but laughably wrong: “A tennis serve simulator is rolling on the walkway,” “A gray hoverboard is driving on the pathway” — both misidentifications of a robot lawn mower.PreviousNext1/3I donned a Ghostface mask to see how the various AIs would react. Nest sent the most useful alert.In my testing, text alerts from Google and Ring provided the most context and specificity, and Apple often didn’t try, saying “someone” rather than providing any detail. For example, it would say “someone is walking in the yard,” whereas Ring and Google provided more context: a delivery person is walking in the yard, a person in uniform, someone carrying a bag, and so on.Apple was also the briefest. For example, when my cat was on the front porch, Apple said, “A cat sat on the porch.” Ring went with “A cat is standing on the pathway outside the porch.” Google Home told me which cat: “A black and white cat walks across the porch.”All three identified delivery trucks, correctly flagging UPS and FedEx vehicles driving past, as well as delivery people approaching the door. Apple was the only one to ID the USPS van pulling up to my mailbox, although not consistently.Google was the most descriptive with vehicles — “a light-colored car drives by on the street” or “a white van,” “a dark-colored SUV” — Apple and Ring mostly said “a vehicle drove by,” sometimes with a type (van, car, truck).Apple’s reduce notifications feature combines several alerts into one.These were difficult to read and not terribly useful.Apple’s descriptions were the hardest to digest at a glance, particularly the combined ones through reduce notifications. For example, “Someone seen. Someone carried a box” is clunky. Ring and Google merge the events more fluidly into “a person carried a box up the driveway.”In fairness, Apple Intelligence in Home only officially launched this month, so I expect this to improve, but as things stand, Ring’s and Google’s are more useful and cost less.Finicky facial recognition and alertsFor a doorbell camera, the real advantage of AI descriptions is knowing who’s there right away. All three offer facial recognition alongside the ability to spot a UPS driver or similar.Ring was the most consistently accurate, identifying me every time I approached the door. Apple hedged its bets, sometimes identifying me, sometimes saying “Someone who may be Jennifer Pattison Tuohy,” and other times just “Someone.” Google got it right about half the time; the other half it thought I was my daughter’s best mate (a change from the UPS driver it pegged me as for most of last year).Apple just wasn’t sure about me.Ring was the most accurate; Google was mostly accurate.Text descriptions are more useful if they show up, and quickly. But on the doorbell camera I was testing, Apple’s often didn’t. Apple Home reliably alerted me when someone pressed the doorbell, and it recorded every event, but notifications about other motion events were inconsistent.A potential issue here is that, unlike its competition, Apple doesn’t control the whole experience. HomeKit Secure Video only works with third-party hardware — there are no Apple cameras yet. I was using the G400, Aqara’s latest wired doorbell camera.When I first set it up, alerts arrived in Apple Home with no issues, but at some point they stopped, and no amount of troubleshooting brought them back. However, alerts kept coming through in the Aqara app. I also still got doorbell ring alerts in the Home app, and notifications from other Aqara cameras continued to work.The Google Nest doorbell captured everything and was consistently first to notify me of an event. Ring was also fast and mostly reliable; its notifications showed up just after Google’s, though I’d occasionally get “This video is unavailable” when trying to play back footage.Reliability is Apple’s biggest fix, plus some innovationThe good news is that recording in HomeKit Secure Video has improved significantly with iOS 27. Apple said it completely rearchitected the system, which addresses a long-standing problem with missing clips.I’ve noticed that cameras load faster, are more stable, and no longer miss recordings. An Eve outdoor camera that was almost always offline has been stable since the upgrade, and the Aqara Camera Hub G5 outdoor camera and G350 indoor camera have also been solid. The G400 doorbell camera has been the only problem child, with missing notifications, but it records consistently.All the other HomeKit cameras I tested reliably sent alerts; only the Aqara doorbell camera had the issue, but even when I didn’t get alerts, I could use video search to find events.Typing “When did the USPS truck come” in the Apple Home app pulled up every instance the Aqara doorbell spotted the mail delivery. In comparison, while the Nest Cam didn’t identify the USPS truck as often, its video search results contained more specifics, including an event where the mail person dropped off an Amazon package.Of the three, Google’s video search was the most useful, followed by Ring’s, then Apple’s, which directly correlates with the amount of detail each provides in the text descriptions.Apple has two features Ring and Google don’t offer. The first is clip stitching, where Apple Intelligence identifies someone or something on one camera, recognizes it again on another, understands these are related, and plays the sequence as a single video in the Home app. I haven’t found a real use for this so far, but it’s been fun for tracking my dog around the house when I’m out.The second feature is bringing events that Apple judges important to the top of the search box. In the last two weeks, it’s only highlighted the trash pickup ━ I guess my life just isn’t that noteworthy.Here’s where Ring winsOne of the biggest problems with security cameras is filtering out the important info from the sheer volume of everything they see. Even with AI notifications turned on, I still get a stream of alerts from Apple Home and Google Home. Some are more useful than they used to be, but overload is still an issue.These are the only alerts Ring sent from the doorbell camera over an entire weekend when I had Unusual Event enabled.Apple’s noteworthy events is a similar concept, but it doesn’t send a specific alert instead just surfacing the clip to the top of your search page.While Apple’s noteworthy events feature shows promise, Ring’s Unusual Event feature is the best solution I’ve seen. It learns what normal traffic looks like for each camera, then notifies you only when something isn’t normal. This summer, I cut my Ring notifications down from around 40 a day to just two or three.Instead of getting an alert every time my cat is on my porch, I only get one when a raccoon or possum walks by. It doesn’t send alerts when my son comes home from school, but it does when he comes home at 2AM. The camera by my chicken coop no longer sends a series of notifications when someone is feeding them or collecting eggs — but it does alert me when I am out there at midnight with a flashlight to wrestle a snake.What’s next: cameras that can actThe cats were a big fan of Google Home’s inability to tell them apart, as it meant more kibble. (This is not Smokey).The natural progression here is automations triggered by the camera understanding what it sees. Turn on the sprinklers if there’s a raccoon in the backyard, but not if it’s just my dog. A cat at the back door broadcasts an alert through my smart speakers so someone can let them in. The trash truck rolling past without stopping sends an urgent notification to put the bins out before it comes back the other way.This is where cameras move beyond being simply security devices to become intelligent smart-home sensors that can understand what’s happening and potentially act on it.Google Home recently added the ability to trigger automations from camera alerts, although in my early testing, it’s not reliable enough.I tried it with my three cats and a pet feeder using Google’s new Pet Memory feature. But instead of only dispensing food for one specific cat as I asked, it triggered every time it saw a cat. At least the cats were happy.The problem is accuracy. When AI can’t reliably identify the subject, the automations can’t respond reliably. So, my earlier example of Apple accurately recognizing the USPS van half the time would mean any automation I set up to alert me the mail is here would only work half the time.Today, Apple doesn’t have this capability, but if the rumors that the company is developing its own video doorbell and security camera are true, I would expect to see a feature like this come to Apple Home.The privacy tradeoffThe smarter cameras become, the more they need to know about your home. For a system to understand what’s normal, it needs to learn who lives there, when they come and go, which pets are around, and which vehicles belong. This raises very real concerns around privacy and surveillance.Ring has faced particular scrutiny over its cloud-based architecture and partnerships with law enforcement. Where Google and Apple can start with local processing, Ring processes all footage in the cloud by default.There’s real benefit in a system knowing everything about my home — I’d just prefer to be the only one who knows it.Last month, Ring announced an overhaul to that model, introducing a new default encryption system called TAKE. This rotates encryption keys for cloud-stored video and deletes Ring’s copy after 24 hours. Among other privacy protections, including no admin access, Ring says this means it can no longer hand over decrypted footage to the police. However, it can still be compelled to provide encrypted files.With Apple’s standard HomeKit Secure Video, your home hub processes footage locally and encrypts it end-to-end before sending it to the cloud for storage. But adding Apple Intelligence changes that: Video summaries are now processed in the cloud using Apple’s Private Cloud Compute (PCC), where they are unencrypted for processing.According to Apple, PCC writes the captions, sends them back, and then “permanently deletes the data from PCC.” Apple support docs also state that there is no admin access, and nothing identifies who the footage belongs to.RelatedOur picks for the best privacy-focused video doorbellsThe best smart doorbell camerasCameras get an Apple Intelligence boost in Apple HomeGoogle takes a similar approach to Apple, but without end-to-end encryption; footage is encrypted in transit and at rest. Gemini for Home-enabled Nest cameras can use some on-device processing, but the heavy work is done in the Gemini cloud, in line with Google Home’s privacy practices.A big question for me is whether all this intelligence has to live on someone else’s computers. There’s real benefit in a system knowing everything about my home — I’d just prefer to be the only one who knows it. For privacy, security, and potentially speed, local AI processing and storage feels like the right answer. Manufacturers including Anker Eufy, Reolink, Ubiquiti UniFi, and UGreen already have or have announced products that do this.With a new Apple TV, HomePod, and a possible smart display all rumored to be imminent, Apple’s next generation of hardware might shift more processing back into the house — which could mean paying less every month for the privilege.When Ghostface is at my door, I want Apple Home to tell me.Is Apple Intelligence worth it?Based on my testing of the beta and the initial full release, Apple Intelligence in Home has brought substantial improvements, finally putting HomeKit Secure Video in contention with Ring and Google.Whether it’s worth the price depends on how many cameras you own. If you have one — say, a video doorbell — Apple Intelligence is a reasonable deal at $10 a month if you also need 2TB of iCloud storage. You get competent descriptions, better video search, and Apple’s privacy position. Even with multiple cameras, you can get some benefit by enabling it on just one.Next let’s make them better at telling us what actually matters.However, if you want AI capabilities across your home, including clip stitching, the math gets bad fast. At five cameras, you’re paying $60 a month for Apple to tell you “a cat sat on the porch” or “a vehicle drove by.” The competition gives you more detailed descriptions on as many cameras as you own for $20 a month.Today, you’re paying an Apple premium for less. But this is Apple’s first move, and I expect it to improve. AI has unlocked genuine utility here, making security cameras better at telling us what’s happening; next, let’s make them better at telling us what actually matters.A few years ago, a “motion detected” alert wasn’t enough to tell me that my chickens were in trouble. Today, AI can tell me it’s a dog chasing a chicken. The next step is for it to understand that this is something I need to know right now and make sure I get that information quickly enough to act. Eventually, an intelligent home might actually be able to do something about it, too.That’s the smart home I want. But we’re not there yet.Photos and screenshots by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

items.titleZh: 苹果Home的AI摄像头功能能否超越亚马逊和谷歌？我进行了实测
items.descriptionZh:
几年前，作者在复活节捡蛋活动中收到安全摄像头“检测到运动”通知，未加理会，回家后发现四只宠物鸡被自家边境梗犬咬死。回看录像，鸡舍门被鸡推开，而他因匆忙未关好。如果第一条通知不是“检测到运动”，而是“小狗在追鸡”，他可能及时赶回救下鸡。这个亲身经历引出文章主题：AI 生成的文本描述正在改变安全摄像头，让通知从简单运动触发变成一句语义描述，并且几乎即时到达，远早于视频画面加载。

技术原理上，主流安防厂商 Ring、Google Nest、Blink、Wyze、Arlo 现在都提供文本描述，把传统运动触发与视觉语言模型结合。Apple 则在 iOS 27 中通过 Apple Intelligence for Home 将这一能力带入 HomeKit Secure Video。文章测试了 Apple、Ring、Google 三家的 AI 摄像头，主要聚焦视频门铃：Ring Wired Doorbell Pro（249.99 美元）、Google Nest Doorbell 2K（199.99 美元），以及 Apple 侧兼容 HomeKit Secure Video 的 Aqara Doorbell Camera G400（99 美元）。测试关注通知速度、描述准确性和有用性、事件捕获可靠性，也测试了跨摄像头搜索与拼接、异常事件、基于摄像头内容的自动化等功能。

Apple Intelligence 需要 iCloud+ 计划、兼容 HomeKit Secure Video 的摄像头、运行 HomePod/tvOS 27 的 Apple Home Hub，以及支持 AI 的 iPhone 和 iOS 27。功能包括文本描述、自然语言视频搜索、突出“值得注意”的事件、跨摄像头片段拼接，以及把相关事件合并为一条更新通知的“减少通知”。它默认开启减少通知，默认关闭视频摘要。价格方面，2TB iCloud+ 每月 9.99 美元支持一台摄像头，6TB 每月 29.99 美元支持两台，12TB 每月 59.99 美元最多支持五台；没有任何层级支持超过五台摄像头。标准 HomeKit Secure Video 录制另需 iCloud+，起价每月 0.99 美元支持一台 50GB，2.99 美元支持五台 200GB，9.99 美元支持无限 2TB；含 Apple Intelligence 的层级仍可在无限摄像头上使用基本 HomeKit Secure Video 功能。对比之下，Google Home 的 Nest 摄像头以每月 20 美元提供 Gemini 文本描述、视频搜索、面部识别、每日 Home Brief 摘要，覆盖无限摄像头，有线型号还可 24/7 录制。Ring 同样每月 20 美元，提供 AI 文本描述、视频搜索、面部识别、异常事件警报和无限摄像头剪辑录制，有线型号 24/7 录制每台另加 3 美元。Apple 在单摄像头时价格尚可，但多摄像头场景下最高五台 60 美元/月，而对手 20 美元即可覆盖无限摄像头，价格差距明显。

实际体验中，Google 和 Ring 的文本描述上下文最丰富、最具体，Apple 则往往最简短，常只说“某人”，而不提供更多细节。例如猫在前廊时，Apple 说“一只猫坐在门廊”，Ring 说“一只猫站在门廊外的小路上”，Google 则说“一只黑白猫走过门廊”。三者都能识别 UPS 和 FedEx 车辆及快递员，Apple 偶尔是唯一识别出 USPS 面包车开近邮箱的，但并不稳定；Google 对车辆描述最详细。Apple 的合并通知也较生硬，例如“有人被看到。有人拿着箱子”，而 Ring 和 Google 会合并成“一个人把箱子搬上车道”。面部识别方面，Ring 最一致准确，Google 约一半正确，Apple 有时识别出作者，有时说“可能是 Jennifer Pattison Tuohy”，有时只说“某人”。通知可靠性上，Google Nest 最快且捕获完整，Ring 也快且大多可靠，Apple 门铃按下时通知可靠，但其他运动事件通知不一致；Aqara G400 曾停止发送通知。不过 iOS 27 重构了 HomeKit Secure Video，录制稳定性显著改善，摄像头加载更快、不再漏录，其他 HomeKit 摄像头也较稳定。视频搜索中，Google 最有用，Ring 次之，Apple 第三，这与三者文本描述的详细程度直接相关。Apple 独有跨摄像头片段拼接和重要事件置顶，但作者认为实用性有限，后者过去两周只突出了垃圾回收。

items.title: Intel expects 14A to be 'within 5%' the performance of TSMC's A14
items.description: Intel's Naga Chandrasekaran now claims that Intel 14A node will deliver performance 'within 5%' of TSMC's A14 technology, a claim that requires a closer examination.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Intel's 14A (1.4nm-class) process technology is expected to deliver performance 'within 5%' of TSMC's A14 (1.4nm-class) production node, Naga Chandrasekaran, the chief technology and operations officer as well as general manager of Intel Foundry, told investment banking firm KeyBanc (via @Alex_Intel_). Given TSMC's track record of delivering steady performance, power, and area (PPA) gains with every new node, this might sound like entirely good news. However, the statement deserves a closer examination.Delivering 'within 5%' performance is an ambiguous statement that may mean that 14A will be 5% faster than A14, or that 14A will be 5% slower than A14. While 'within 5%' performance compared to the direct rival of the same class may sound like a good competitive position, in recent years Intel's process technologies trailed TSMC's nodes in transistor density and remained competitive in performance or power. This was, to a large degree, attributed to Intel's historic focus on CPU performance, but not necessarily transistor density, as its own fabs have offset additional costs associated with larger dies.In fact, actual shipping processors suggest Intel's 18A is at least competitive with TSMC's N2 in maximum achievable CPU frequency as Intel's Core Ultra X9 388H 'Panther Lake' can hit 5.10 GHz (at an 80W max turbo power), AMD's EPYC 9586F has the highest single-core clock of 5.0 GHz (at a default 500W CPU power), Apple's A20 Pro can achieve 4.93 GHz, whereas Apple's M6 can hit 4.78 GHz. These numbers should not be converted directly into a statement such as '18A is X% faster than N2,' because the processors use different architectures, voltages, standard-cell libraries, thermal envelopes, and physical implementations. However, they do provide a useful real-world reference point: the available N2 processors do not show a substantial frequency advantage over 18A. If anything, the highest observed CPU frequencies favor Intel's process.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Based on internal estimates, Intel officially states that compared to its already fast 18A, its 14A is expected to provide 15% – 20% higher performance at the same power, or 25% – 35% lower power at the same frequency and transistor count. By contrast, TSMC expects its A14 to be 10% - 15% faster than N2 at the same power, or 25% - 30% lower power at the same clocks and transistor count.Combining the observed 18A and N2 CPU frequencies of Intel's 18A and TSMC's N2 with Intel's stated 15% – 20% 14A gain and TSMC's assumed 10% – 15% A14 gain would ordinarily suggest a modest 14A performance advantage of A14 even in most conservative scenarios for Intel. Therefore, Intel's new expectation that 14A will be 'within 5%' of A14 is notably less ambitious than one might infer from the company's published process specifications, even though the 'within 5%' statement does not tell us which process Intel expects to lead. Swipe to scroll horizontally Scenario Intel 14A gain vs. 18A TSMC A14 gain vs. N2 14A extrapolation from 5.10 GHz A14 extrapolation from 4.788 GHz Implied 14A advantage Intel worstTSMC best 15% 15% 5.865 5.506 6.50% Both minimum gains 15% 10% 5.865 5.267 11.40% Both maximum gains 20% 15% 6.12 5.506 11.20% Intel bestTSMC worst 20% 10% 6.12 5.267 16.20% Starting points: Intel 18A = 5.10 GHz (Core Ultra 9 388H); TSMC N2 = 4.78 GHz (Apple M6).Using Apple's M6 as the real-world N2 reference, a similar calculation gives Intel 14A a 6.5% – 16.2% implied advantage over TSMC A14. Even the worst possible combination for Intel — 14A achieves only +15% while A14 achieves the full +15% — puts Intel's node well beyond the 'within 5%' estimate given by Naga Chandrasekaran.It should be clearly noted that our calculations do not predict 14A or A14 CPU frequencies, as we use clocks from current CPU architectures with improvement claims for upcoming process technologies. The calculation is useful primarily for illustrating what the companies' published numbers imply relative to today's products.Intel's 'within 5%' assessment raises an interesting question: why does Intel expect 14A and A14 to be so close when the companies' published process gains appear to suggest a larger gap? Perhaps Intel's assessment incorporates factors that these simple calculations do not capture. Or perhaps the head of Intel Foundry took a page from his boss Lip-Bu Tan's book and now prefers to underpromise. items.titleZh: Intel expects 14A to be 'within 5%' the performance of TSMC's A14
items.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware 报道，Intel Foundry 首席技术与运营官兼总经理 Naga Chandrasekaran 向投资银行 KeyBanc 表示，Intel 的 14A（1.4nm 级）工艺预计性能将落在台积电 A14（1.4nm 级）的“5%以内”。这句话看似说明 Intel 已接近台积电下一代节点，但表述本身有歧义：14A 可能比 A14 快 5%，也可能慢 5%。考虑到台积电历来能在每代节点上稳定交付性能、功耗和面积（PPA）提升，这一说法值得进一步审视。

背景方面，近年来 Intel 工艺在晶体管密度上落后于台积电，但在性能或功耗上仍保持竞争力。文章认为，这在很大程度上源于 Intel 历史上更关注 CPU 性能而非晶体管密度，同时 Intel 自有晶圆厂可以抵消较大芯片面积带来的额外成本。实际出货处理器也显示，Intel 18A 至少在最高 CPU 频率上与台积电 N2 有竞争力：Intel Core Ultra X9 388H“Panther Lake”可在 80W 最大加速功耗下达到 5.10 GHz；AMD EPYC 9586F 在默认 500W 下达到 5.0 GHz 单核最高频率；Apple A20 Pro 可达 4.93 GHz，Apple M6 可达 4.78 GHz。文章强调，不能把这些数字直接换算成“18A 比 N2 快 X%”，因为不同处理器采用不同架构、电压、标准单元库、热设计功耗和物理实现。但它们提供了现实参考：现有 N2 处理器并未显示出明显频率优势，最高观测频率反而对 Intel 工艺有利。

根据 Intel 内部估计，14A 相比已经较快的 18A，可在相同功耗下提升 15%–20% 性能，或在相同频率和晶体管数量下降低 25%–35% 功耗。台积电则预计 A14 在相同功耗下比 N2 快 10%–15%，或在相同频率和晶体管数量下降低 25%–30% 功耗。若把当前 18A 和 N2 处理器的最高频率，与两家公司公布的等功耗性能提升幅度结合推算，通常会得出 14A 相对 A14 有一定优势，即使采用对 Intel 最保守的假设也是如此。因此，Intel 现在称 14A 将在 A14 的“5%以内”，比从其公布工艺规格中可推断出的预期要保守得多，尽管“5%以内”并未说明 Intel 预计谁领先。

文章用两组起点进行了推算。第一组以 Intel 18A = 5.10 GHz（Core Ultra 9 388H）、台积电 N2 = 5.00 GHz（EPYC 9586F）为起点：在“Intel 最差、台积电最好”的场景下，即 14A 比 18A 提升 15%、A14 比 N2 提升 15%，14A 推算频率为 5.865 GHz，A14 为 5.75 GHz，隐含 14A 领先约 2.0%；在双方都取最小提升时领先约 6.6%；双方都取最大提升时领先约 6.4%；在“Intel 最好、台积电最差”时领先约 11.3%。因此，按官方等功耗性能预测，14A 对 A14 的潜在性能优势约为 2%–11.3%，具体取决于假设组合。

第二组以 Apple M6 的 4.788 GHz 作为 N2 现实参考：在 Intel 最差、台积电最好场景下，14A 对 A14 隐含优势约 6.5%；双方最小提升时约 11.4%；双方最大提升时约 11.2%；Intel 最好、台积电最差时约 16.2%。也就是说，若用 Apple M6 作为 N2 参考，Intel 14A 对台积电 A14 的隐含优势可达 6.5%–16.2%。即便采用对 Intel 最不利的组合——14A 仅提升 15%，而 A14 达到完整 15% 提升——Intel 节点仍然超出 Chandrasekaran 所说的“5%以内”。

文章同时明确，这些计算并不是在预测 14A 或 A14 的实际 CPU 频率，而是用当前 CPU 架构的频率，加上两家公司对即将到来的工艺技术的改进声明，来展示其公布数字相对当今产品意味着什么。Intel 的“5%以内”评估引出一个问题：为什么 Intel 预计 14A 和 A14 会如此接近，而两家公司公布的工艺增益似乎暗示更大差距？一种可能是 Intel 的评估纳入了这些简单计算未捕捉的因素；另一种可能是，Intel Foundry 负责人借鉴其上司陈立武（Lip-Bu Tan）的风格，如今更倾向于少承诺、留余地。总体而言，14A 是 Intel Foundry 与台积电 A14 竞争的关键节点；若真能落在 A14 的 5%以内，将意味着 Intel 回到与台积电同一梯队，但按公开规格推算，14A 的潜力可能被低估，最终仍需实际产品验证。

items.title: New Jersey hits Microsoft-linked AI data center with record fine for 62 unpermitted power generators, issues 45-day shutdown deadline
items.description: The DataOne data center is facing a record fine of $1.07 million for operating portable turbine generators without permission. Residents say that the penalty is a drop in the bucket for these big tech companies.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The DataOne data center in Vineland, New Jersey, has just been hit with a record $1.07 million fine for operating unpermitted portable generators on the construction site. According to the New York Times, state inspectors spotted 62 of these units powering the facility back in late July.Residents had already complained about it at a February town hall meeting. Inspectors said that there were no generators on site when they first visited in December last year. However, some residents said that “some type of unit” was spotted by satellite imagery back in February, leading to their complaint at the community assembly.Residents of Vineland have already made multiple complaints about the development. Some of the issues t include the unpermitted construction of a 1.5-million-gallon LNG tank and unacceptable noise levels, especially at night, that affected homes within a half-mile radius of the construction site. They also said that there was little to no public consultation on the project before it went into full swing, with the people only finding out that a data center was being constructed in their neighborhood after Microsoft announced a $33 billion deal with Nebius, which in turn contracted DataOne to supply the compute they need.Despite a record fine, some residents feel that the punishment isn’t enough. “It’s a ‘don’t ask for permission, just ask for forgiveness later’ kind of deal,” longtime Vineland resident Steve Brown told the Times. He also added, “It’s still kind of a drop in the bucket for a company that has several billion dollars of capital.” Long-time community member Tiffany Leone-Vespa also added, “What’s $1.07 million? They should have done it for each generator they were running illegally. They’re billionaires. It’s like pocket change.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: On the other hand, DataOne disagreed with the fine. A company spokesperson said that “We will apply for the air permits for the temporary generators,” and also added that it’s transitioning from the polluting and noisy portable turbines to more modern fuel cells. New Jersey ordered it to comply with the permitting requirements and to stop using the generators if they’re not granted within 45 days.This is a similar situation that the citizens of Memphis and Southaven faced when SpaceXAI deployed 69 unpermitted generators to provide power to its Colossus 2 data center. It has become the subject of a lawsuit, especially as the community raised concerns that they were spewing thousands of tons of pollutants in the primarily black neighborhood. However, the Department of Justice stepped in and asked the court to dismiss the case because the site “supports mission-critical operations.” Elon Musk’s company eventually agreed to remove all unpermitted turbines, but said that the process will take over a year as replacement 1.2-gigawatt plants gradually come online. items.titleZh: 新泽西州对与微软有关联的AI数据中心开出创纪录罚单，因其62台未经许可的发电机，并下达45天关闭期限
items.descriptionZh:
新泽西州 Vineland 的 DataOne 数据中心因在建设现场运行 62 台未获许可的便携式发电机，被州监管机构开出创纪录的 107 万美元罚单。这一事件把 AI 数据中心高速扩张与地方环境、噪音、许可审批和社区知情权之间的矛盾推到了台前。背景是微软与 Nebius 达成 330 亿美元算力协议，Nebius 又委托 DataOne 提供所需算力；但当地居民表示，他们直到相关交易公布后，才发现社区附近正在建设数据中心，事前几乎没有公众咨询。

时间线显示，州检查员称去年 12 月首次到访时现场还没有发电机，但居民称今年 2 月卫星图像中已能看到“某种设备”，并在 2 月的镇民大会上提出投诉。到 7 月底，检查员发现共有 62 台便携式发电机在为该设施供电。居民此前还投诉该项目未经许可建设 150 万加仑的液化天然气储罐，以及尤其夜间不可接受的噪音，影响范围达到施工现场半英里半径内的住宅。液化天然气储罐用于把天然气冷却液化后储存，体积可缩小约 600 倍，便于运输和现场供气，但涉及易燃物安全和空气排放许可，不能随意建设。

从技术原理看，AI 数据中心需要数百兆瓦甚至吉瓦级的连续电力，而电网接入、变电站建设和排放许可往往需要较长时间。便携式燃气发电机或燃气轮机可以模块化、快速部署，通过燃烧天然气驱动涡轮或活塞发电，满足建设期或临时算力上线的电力缺口。但燃烧过程会产生氮氧化物、颗粒物、一氧化碳和二氧化碳，并伴随较大噪音。DataOne 表示不同意罚款，将申请临时发电机的空气许可，并称正从污染和噪音较大的便携式涡轮转向更现代的燃料电池。燃料电池通过电化学反应将燃料化学能直接转化为电能，不经过燃烧，因此氮氧化物和颗粒物排放更低、噪音更小、效率也较高；若使用天然气，仍会有二氧化碳排放，且需要燃料供应、水管理和空气许可，但相比便携式燃气机组是更清洁的分布式供电路线。

罚款数字本身也引发争议。107 万美元分摊到 62 台发电机，约合每台 1.73 万美元。居民 Steve Brown 称这是“先不申请许可，之后再求原谅”的做法，并认为对拥有数十亿美元资本的公司来说仍是九牛一毛。Tiffany Leone-Vespa 更直言：“107 万美元算什么？应该按每台非法运行的发电机来罚。他们是亿万富翁，这就像零钱。”新泽西州已命令 DataOne 在 45 天内满足许可要求，否则必须停止使用这些发电机。

类似冲突也出现在孟菲斯和 Southaven。马斯克旗下公司——原文称 SpaceXAI，通常指 xAI——曾为 Colossus 2 数据中心部署 69 台未获许可的发电机，引发诉讼，社区担心这些设备向以黑人为主的社区排放数千吨污染物。美国司法部后来介入，以该站点“支持关键任务运营”为由请求法院驳回案件。该公司最终同意移除所有未许可涡轮，但表示替换的 1.2 吉瓦发电厂逐步上线需要一年以上。相关报道还显示，威斯康星州居民也因噪音对微软相关 AI 数据中心提起集体诉讼，说明超大规模 AI 算力设施与周边社区的摩擦正在增多。

总体来看，这一事件的核心不只是罚款，而是 AI 算力竞赛下的电力瓶颈与监管滞后。为了快速上线 GPU 集群，数据中心开发商可能倾向使用现场燃气发电和液化天然气设施，绕过漫长电网排队和审批；但这类方案把排放、噪音和安全外部性转嫁给附近居民，并容易引发环境正义和诉讼风险。DataOne 转向燃料电池、新泽西设定 45 天合规期限，以及 Colossus 2 用 1.2 吉瓦电厂替换未许可涡轮，都表明行业正在被迫从“先部署、后补票”转向更合规的供电方案。未来，AI 数据中心的竞争力不仅取决于芯片和算力，也取决于能否在电网升级、储能、燃料电池、清洁发电和社区沟通之间找到可被监管与公众接受的平衡。

items.title: Google's orbital AI data center test packs four TPUs and 1,000W of solar power
items.description: Google will launch an experimental satellite into orbit on October 1, taking four tensor processing units with it.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Google is set to launch an experimental satellite, named MVP, into orbit next week to test running an AI data center in space. As part of a wider initiative called Project Suncatcher, the satellite will be aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket when it launches from the Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. Once in space, and assuming everything goes well, the tech on board the satellite will be capable of handling simple AI requests from space.The New York Times points out that while the move is an important one, the satellite will be limited in terms of its processing power. It will feature just four Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) and be similar to a single Earth-bound server in terms of capabilities. It will be powered by solar panels capable of providing a single kilowatt of power to the tensor chips.While clearly limited, the orbiting server is set to handle AI requests for up to a year, although it will remain in orbit for up to six years. After that, gravity will take hold, and the satellite will burn up during re-entry into Earth's atmosphere.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Before that happens, James Manyika, Google's senior vice president of research, expects to learn more about how space may become a home for future data centers, though probably not for a long time.“We don’t expect, to be perfectly frank, that we’ll have anything usefully operational in the next few years,” the SVP told the Times. He went on to compare the venture to Google's driverless cars, saying that Google was testing those "like 15 years before anything showed up." The idea of users accessing a version of Gemini running in space is some way from coming to fruition. You may like China launches 'Supercomputing-1' AI satellite as orbital data centers gather momentum Intel's proposed two-tier satellite network puts the brains of satellite constellations in higher orbit Google reportedly developing 'Frozen v2' chip with Gemini's architecture etched into the silicon — engineers project 6 to 10 times more tokens per watt than latest TPUs But it's also something that Google and other companies are set to investigate further. Alongside Google, Elon Musk (xAI, Tesla, SpaceX), as well as Jeff Bezos (Amazon) and Sam Altman (OpenAI), have been making noises about the prospect of orbital data centers for some time now. China has already put its own AI compute into orbit. Even Intel has a patent for orbital data centers of its own.Putting servers into space does have its issues, not least the problem of getting them there. Radiation and computers don't get along, and the radiation found in space can cause "bit flips" that change the way chips process data. Google's answer, for now, is to restart the chips every so often to reset them. The company has also devised a cooling system that will vent heat directly into space — since the usual fan-based solution simply won't work without any air.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsDespite these accommodations, the four chips in Google's test satellite will still get too hot, too quickly. They'll only be able to run for around 15 minutes before they need to be shut down to allow them to cool off.Regardless, it's still early days for the concept of running servers in space. Google plans to launch a pair of satellites next, with long-term plans for networked fleets of more than 80 satellites also already floated.By Manyika's estimation, Google has 15 years to go from a four-chip server to a full-on data center. The clock is ticking. Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, oradd us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

items.titleZh: 谷歌轨道AI数据中心测试：搭载四个TPU和1000瓦太阳能供电
items.descriptionZh:
谷歌计划在下周发射一颗名为 MVP 的实验卫星，作为“Project Suncatcher”计划的一部分，测试在太空中运行 AI 数据中心。该卫星将搭乘 SpaceX 的 Falcon 9 火箭，从加州范登堡太空军基地升空。如果一切顺利，星上技术将能够从太空处理简单的 AI 请求。不过《纽约时报》指出，这颗卫星的处理能力有限：它仅搭载四个张量处理单元（TPU），整体能力大致相当于地球上的一台服务器，由可提供 1 千瓦功率的太阳能板供电。该轨道服务器将处理 AI 请求最长约一年，但会在轨停留最长六年，之后受重力影响再入地球大气层并烧毁。

技术挑战方面，太空辐射会导致“位翻转”，改变芯片处理数据的方式；谷歌目前的应对办法是定期重启芯片以进行重置。冷却方面，由于太空中没有空气，传统风扇散热无法工作，谷歌设计了直接将热量排放到太空的冷却系统。但即便如此，四颗芯片仍会很快过热，只能运行约 15 分钟，就需要关机冷却。这些限制表明，太空 AI 服务器仍处于非常早期的实验阶段。

谷歌研究高级副总裁 James Manyika 表示，坦率地说，不指望未来几年内会有真正有实用价值的系统投入运行。他将这一尝试比作谷歌的无人驾驶汽车项目：谷歌在相关技术真正出现前约 15 年就开始测试。用户访问运行在太空中的 Gemini 版本，距离实现仍很遥远。不过，谷歌和其他公司预计会继续探索轨道数据中心。马斯克旗下的 xAI、Tesla、SpaceX，以及贝索斯的 Amazon 和奥特曼的 OpenAI，都曾提出类似设想；中国也已将自己的 AI 算力送入轨道，Intel 则拥有轨道数据中心相关专利。

按照谷歌的规划，下一步将发射两颗卫星，长期目标则是建立由超过 80 颗卫星组成的联网舰队。Manyika 估计，从目前的四芯片服务器发展到完整数据中心，大约还需要 15 年。总体来看，这次 MVP 卫星任务是一次关键但能力有限的在轨验证，旨在为未来太空数据中心积累辐射、散热、供电和 AI 推理等方面的经验。

history.content: Yesterday, with a little prodding, it was discovered that Meta’s Muse would expose its filesystem to curious users. The files offered a fascinating peek under the hood of an AI chatbot, and appeared to expose details we weren’t meant to see, not least because Muse itself told people, including us, it wasn’t supposed to reveal them.But today Muse will eagerly offer up the contents of its file system when you ask for it. That appears to be because, as Meta’s Nat Friedman later said, this is the “intended behavior.”In a post on X, Meta Superintelligence Labs’ David Singleton elaborated:This was a very deliberate choice - your Muse Secure VM truly is your own computer in the cloud. You can install software in it, write and compile code, use the browser to surf the web: it is your own Linux box that you can operate as you choose with your Muse.Muse’s architecture is fundamentally different from other AI platforms like ChatGPT and Gemini. It’s closer to running OpenClaw on a local machine, except the machine is in the cloud.In a statement provided to The Verge yesterday, Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts said, “We’re continuing to make updates to the product, so users may see changes in how much information is available about their virtual machine.” And that seems to be the case. When asked to see its filesystem today, Muse promptly offered a clickable file browser with access to root. Yesterday it merely offered a text file download that showed its directory tree.Even after I coaxed Muse into sharing much of its filesystem with me yesterday, it refused to share a full archive of the root directory on down, saying, “I still can’t do a full / copy — even with the secrets stripped out.” Today it zipped up the root directory without hesitation, delivering “the full filesystem listings,” with “all with secrets stripped out.”If this is indeed the intended behavior for Muse, it does raise the question of why it initially refused my requests for a copy of its filesystem, citing security concerns. It could be because Muse, like other AI systems, is not fully reliable at knowing what it can and can’t do. Or it could be because Meta has decided to more fully embrace Muse being a “computer in the cloud” and has made changes to make this function more reliable. In any event, it’s pretty fun.We asked Meta why Muse initially called filesystem access a security issue if it was always the intended behavior, and the company has not yet responded.
history.author: Terrence O’Brien
history.titleZh: Meta让Muse文件系统更加易于访问
history.descriptionZh:
Meta 的 AI 聊天机器人 Muse 近日因文件系统访问权限引发关注。起初，用户发现 Muse 会暴露其文件系统，让人得以窥见 AI 聊天机器人底层结构，甚至看到一些似乎不应公开的细节；Muse 自己也曾表示不应透露这些内容。但仅过一天，Muse 便会在用户要求时直接提供文件系统内容。Meta 的 Nat Friedman 随后称，这其实是“预期行为”。Meta Superintelligence Labs 的 David Singleton 在 X 上进一步解释：这是刻意设计，用户的 Muse Secure VM 确实是“云中属于自己的计算机”。用户可以在其中安装软件、编写和编译代码、使用浏览器上网，它是一台可由用户通过 Muse 自主操作的 Linux 机器。

从技术架构看，Muse 与 ChatGPT、Gemini 等主流 AI 平台有根本差异。后两者通常不向用户暴露底层文件系统，而 Muse 更接近在本地机器上运行 OpenClaw，只不过这台机器位于云端。Muse 的核心创新在于，把聊天机器人与用户专属的安全虚拟机结合起来，让 AI 不只是对话界面，也成为操作云中 Linux 环境的代理。用户可获得 root 访问权限，查看、下载甚至打包文件系统。文中未给出具体延迟、吞吐等性能参数，主要变化体现在访问方式和权限控制上。

对比前一天与今天的行为，变化明显。昨天，Muse 仅提供显示目录树的文本文件下载；即使被引导分享大部分文件系统，也拒绝提供从根目录以下的完整归档，理由是安全考虑，并称“即使剥离秘密，也不能做完整的 / 复制”。今天，Muse 则迅速提供可点击的文件浏览器，可直接访问 root，并毫不犹豫地将根目录打包，提供“完整文件系统列表”，且“所有秘密都已剥离”。Meta 发言人 Daniel Roberts 曾对 The Verge 表示，公司会继续更新产品，因此用户可能看到虚拟机可用信息量的变化。这一说法与观察到的变化吻合。

若文件系统访问确实是 Muse 的预期行为，那么其最初以安全为由拒绝请求就产生了疑问：这可能说明 Muse 与其他 AI 系统一样，对自身能做什么、不能做什么并不完全可靠；也可能说明 Meta 决定更彻底地把 Muse 定位为“云中计算机”，并调整了相关功能以提高可靠性。Meta 尚未回应为何最初将文件系统访问称为安全问题。

总体而言，Muse 的应用场景包括云端开发、代码编译、软件安装、网页浏览和个性化 AI 环境定制，强调用户对虚拟机的透明控制。但它也带来新的安全与治理挑战：当 AI 代理与用户专属 Linux 环境深度结合时，能力边界、敏感信息隔离和安全策略一致性需要更明确的机制。Muse 的案例显示，Meta 正试图把聊天机器人推向“可操作的云计算机”，而不仅是问答工具；这种定位能否兼顾开放性与安全性，仍有待观察。

history.content: Sony and Universal Music Group filed yet another suit against Suno. The labels claim its new v6 model still infringes on their copyrights because it’s trained on user outputs from previous models, which were themselves trained on unlicensed music ripped from YouTube and other sources. Sony and UMG are notable holdouts who did not sign a licensing agreement with Suno.In its complaint shared with The Verge, Sony and UMG accuse Suno of “model laundering,” saying:“Training a ‘new’ model on the outputs of an infringing model does not eliminate the infringement; it launders it, passing the value of Plaintiffs’ expression from the copied recordings into the tainted models, from those models into their outputs, and from those outputs into v6 … V6 is not a fresh start; it is the fruit of the same poisoned tree.”When v6 launched, Suno’s Jack Brody told The Verge it was “trained from the ground up, with a new set of data,” including “user data,” but did not offer details beyond that. Suno spokesperson Rachel Racusen later confirmed to The Verge that data includes “creations” from users, saying, “v6 was trained on content licensed from our partners, interactions including creations and preference signals from our community, and the accumulated learnings from our team,” but did not specify whether that included uploaded audio or outputs based on uploaded audio.Sony further alleges that Suno used distillation to train v6. It claims that it was trained to replicate the results of its previous, “teacher” models, which were created using infringing data.The complaint says that “even a model not directly trained on Plaintiffs’ recordings is informed by, and benefits from, Suno’s retained unauthorized copies.” Essentially, the labels argue that, unless Suno truly starts from scratch, its models will continue to be built on stolen data.Update September 25th, 2026: Added statement from Suno.

history.titleZh: 索尼和环球音乐再次起诉Suno
history.descriptionZh:
索尼音乐与环球音乐集团（UMG）再次对 AI 音乐生成平台 Suno 提起诉讼，指控其最新 v6 模型仍然侵犯版权。两家唱片公司是与 Suno 未签署授权协议的显著“钉子户”。它们称，v6 并非真正独立的新模型，而是建立在前代模型输出之上，而这些前代模型又是用从 YouTube 等来源抓取的无授权音乐训练的。诉状将这种做法称为“模型洗白”（model laundering）：在侵权模型输出上训练“新”模型不能消除侵权，只是把原告表达的价值从盗版录音传递到受污染模型，再从模型传递到输出，最终进入 v6；“v6 不是全新开始，而是同一棵毒树结出的果实。”

Suno 在 v6 发布时曾由 Jack Brody 表示，v6 是“从零训练，使用新的数据集”，其中包括“用户数据”，但未提供更多细节。发言人 Rachel Racusen 后来向 The Verge 确认，这些数据包括用户的“创作”，并称 v6 训练于合作伙伴授权内容、社区互动（包括创作和偏好信号）以及团队积累的学习成果，但没有说明是否包含用户上传的音频或基于上传音频生成的输出。索尼还指控 Suno 使用蒸馏方法训练 v6，即让 v6 复现此前“教师”模型的结果，而这些教师模型是用侵权数据创建的。诉状称，即使某模型没有直接训练于原告录音，它仍受到 Suno 保留的未授权副本影响并从中获益。本质上，唱片公司认为，除非 Suno 真正从零开始，否则其模型会继续建立在被盗数据之上。

从技术上看，蒸馏通常用于将大型教师模型的能力迁移到更小或新模型中，以降低训练成本、保留输出风格和偏好；但在版权争议中，它可能被用来切断新模型与原始侵权数据之间的直接联系，同时继承由侵权数据获得的能力。这正是所谓“模型洗白”的核心：不是直接复制录音，而是复制由侵权模型学到的表达和偏好。Suno 将 v6 描述为“从零训练、新数据集”，可视为其主张的创新点，但唱片公司质疑这一说法，认为新数据中包含旧模型输出，因此无法净化侵权链条。目前没有披露 v6 的具体性能参数或与前代模型的量化对比数据，争议焦点集中在训练数据来源、模型衍生链和授权合规，而非生成质量本身。

此案的影响超出 Suno 一家。它触及生成式音乐 AI 的关键法律边界：模型迭代时，使用前代模型输出或用户创作作为训练数据，是否需要额外授权；若前代模型本身基于未授权数据，后续模型能否“净化”。若法院支持索尼和 UMG，AI 音乐平台可能被迫对训练数据做更严格溯源，重新谈判许可，或对来自侵权模型和用户输出的训练数据进行隔离。对 Suno 及类似平台而言，未来模型开发、商业化应用和社区创作数据使用政策都将面临更高合规成本。文末更新加入了 Suno 的声明。

history.title: Elon Musk's SpaceXAI to add another 660,000 AI GPUs this year, nearing a total of 1.44 million in operation
history.description: Elon Musk says that the Colossus 2 will receive 220,000 GB300 GPUs by next week, with another two tranches of the same amount expected to arrive later this year. This will put the site at over a million AI GPUs, finally hitting the goal the billionaire set two years ago.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The end goal is finally in sight for Elon Musk, nearly two years after he announced plans to expand the Colossus supercomputer to over a million GPUs. The billionaire said on X that 220,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs will be operational by next week, with another 220,000 coming online in November. He also added that another 220,000 units will come online by late December “if we get lucky.”Colossus 1 is 150k H100, 50k H200 and 30k GB200. Colossus 2 is 110k GB200 and 440k GB300. Another 220k GB300 will be fully operational next week and another 220k in November. If we get lucky, yet another 220k GB300 by late December.September 25, 2026These numbers would add to the 110,000 GB200 and 440,000 GB300 GPUs already operating at Colossus 2, plus the 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200, and 30,000 GB200 GPUs at Colossus 1. This would bring SpaceXAI’s GB300 GPUs to 1.1 million units, with its total GPUs in operation to 1,440,000 units. This is quite an achievement, especially given that the company is behind its rivals by several years — SpaceXAI is only three years old, while Anthropic and OpenAI are six and ten years old, respectively. Interestingly, the Colossus 1 site, which features a combination of Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, is inefficient for training Grok, so Musk rented it out to Anthropic for inference instead. On the other hand, Colossus 2 solely uses Blackwell GPUs, ensuring that there won’t be any bottlenecks.While Elon Musk essentially begged for Jensen Huang to give him these GPUs, getting his hands on them isn’t currently the hardest part. One of the biggest issues facing data center build-outs right now is power, and SpaceXAI solved this by bringing its own. This has resulted in some controversies with the surrounding neighborhood, ending in a lawsuit against the company for running unpermitted gas turbines. It has since promised to remove them, but only over a span of one year as its own 1.2-GW power plant comes online.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Running a million GPUs or more on a single site is an impressive achievement, but SpaceXAI isn’t the only one trying to reach this goal. Broadcom said in 2024 that it has three hyperscale customers gunning for this target by 2027 but didn’t mention who these customers were. As for Elon Musk, the 1-million-GPU target is just the beginning. He said that SpaceXAI will grow its data center capacity sevenfold by 2027, and he’s even aiming for 50 million H100-equivalent GPUs by 2030. These data centers won’t be limited to the ground as well, with SpaceX planning to launch an Orbital Data Center System with a million satellites, despite Jensen Huang saying that it’s a “dream” for now. history.titleZh: Elon Musk's SpaceXAI to add another 660,000 AI GPUs this year, nearing a total of 1.44 million in operation
history.descriptionZh:
马斯克近两年前提出的将 Colossus 超级计算机扩展到超过 100 万块 GPU 的目标，如今已接近实现。他在 X 上表示，下周将有 22 万块 Nvidia GB300 GPU 投入运行，11 月再上线 22 万块；如果顺利，12 月底还会再增加 22 万块。这些新增算力将叠加在现有集群上：Colossus 1 由 15 万 H100、5 万 H200 和 3 万 GB200 组成；Colossus 2 由 11 万 GB200 和 44 万 GB300 组成。按此计算，xAI（原文称 SpaceXAI）的 GB300 总量将达到 110 万块，总 GPU 规模达到 144 万块。

从技术上看，H100/H200 属于 NVIDIA Hopper 架构，GB200/GB300 属于 Grace Blackwell 平台，面向大模型训练和推理，强调 CPU-GPU 协同、高带宽互连和更高能效。Colossus 1 混合使用 Hopper 与 Blackwell，异构组合会给训练带来软件栈、通信和调度瓶颈，因此 xAI 将其租给 Anthropic 用于推理；Colossus 2 则全部采用 Blackwell，避免混合架构瓶颈，更适合训练 Grok 等大规模模型。

这一规模意义显著。xAI 成立仅三年，而 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 已分别成立六年和十年。马斯克能快速堆叠百万级 GPU，说明其算力扩张速度极快。不过，当前数据中心建设的最大瓶颈已不只是 GPU 供应，而是电力。xAI 通过自建供电解决部分问题，但曾因运行未获许可的燃气轮机引发社区争议和诉讼。公司承诺在一年内移除这些设备，同时等待其 1.2 GW 自建电厂上线。

百万 GPU 目标并非 xAI 独有。博通 2024 年称已有三家超大规模客户计划在 2027 年达到类似目标，但未披露名单。对马斯克而言，100 万 GPU 只是起点：他称 xAI 将在 2027 年前把数据中心容量扩大七倍，并计划到 2030 年拥有 5000 万块 H100 等效 GPU。此外，SpaceX 还计划发射由百万颗卫星组成的轨道数据中心系统，尽管黄仁勋认为这目前仍是“梦想”。

整体来看，Colossus 的扩张反映 AI 竞争正进入“吉瓦级电力 + 百万级加速器”的基础设施竞赛阶段。其应用场景包括 Grok 的大规模训练、对外提供推理服务，以及未来可能的轨道计算。关键影响在于，谁能在芯片、网络、电力和散热上同时规模化，谁就可能在下一代大模型竞争中占据优势。

history.title: Meta Muse runs agents on AMD EPYC Turin hosts with two cores and 8GB of memory
history.description: Meta's new Muse AI agent is powered by AMD EPYC Turin hosts, with each user getting a private sandbox with two vCPUs and 8GB of memory.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Meta's new AI agent Muse is powered by AMD EPYC Turin host systems, with each sandbox sporting two dedicated cores and 8GB of memory. Blogger Evan Hoffman and analyst Tae Kim both discovered that Muse will run some rudimentary Ubuntu commands if prompted, passing along the output to help identify things like the specs of the host system. More concerning is that Muse seems able to execute commands that might be unsafe, with Hoffman claiming that Muse offered to set up SSH to Muse's private VM.Imagine if one billion people used a personal AI agent. That's a lot of CPUs and memory pic.twitter.com/ibozUi3a07September 24, 2026Both Kim and Hoffman asked Muse about the VM's specs, and in both instances, Muse revealed that it's running on AMD EPYC 9D25 CPUs, a high-density Turin chip with up to 128 cores. The VMs are running on Ubuntu 24.04 and using Linux kernel 7.0. The systems hosting Muse don't include GPUs. The AI agent revealed that Meta uses separate GPU servers for inference, isolating the agent to CPU-only sandboxes.The agent suggests that each user gets their own private sandbox that's persistent, which allows us to do some math on how many people an individual tray can host. Assuming a 2P system that offers up to 512 vCPUs with 2TB of memory, hosting up to 256 Muse users. Muse has reportedly passed over 500,000 daily active users as of a few days ago, which would come out to somewhere around 2,000 server trays with dual EPYC 9D25 CPUs and 2TB of memory.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: This is just some rough napkin math; don't take it as law. It's possible Meta has CPU-only servers deployed with multiple different chips to host Muse, and it's also possible there's overhead in the configuration. Turin chips support up to 6TB of memory with high-density DIMMs, for instance. Still, EPYC hosts seem popular for this use case, mainly because of their core density, as even a dual-core sandbox can add up quickly when multiplied across hundreds of thousands (or even millions) of users.Muse isn't completely open. Hoffman shared an example where an attempted command failed due to improper permissions when Muse tried to query the kernel buffer. Presumably, sudo (admin) commands would be blocked as well. history.titleZh: Meta Muse runs agents on AMD EPYC Turin hosts with two cores and 8GB of memory
history.descriptionZh:
Meta 新推出的个人 AI 代理 Muse 的底层运行环境和安全边界，近日因博主 Evan Hoffman 与分析师 Tae Kim 的测试而被部分揭开。Muse 目前已作为 Android、iOS 和 macOS 应用上线，其他平台也可通过浏览器和 Meta 账号访问；据报道，其日活跃用户数几天前已突破 50 万。两位测试者发现，Muse 在提示下可以执行部分基础 Ubuntu 命令，并把输出返回给用户，从而帮助推断其宿主系统规格。这暴露出 AI 代理在工具调用和沙箱执行方面的能力，也引发了安全担忧。

测试显示，Muse 运行在 AMD EPYC 9D25 处理器上。该芯片属于 AMD EPYC Turin 高密度产品线，单颗最多 128 个核心。Muse 的虚拟机运行 Ubuntu 24.04 和 Linux 7.0 内核。更关键的是，托管 Muse 的系统本身没有 GPU；Meta 将模型推理放在独立的 GPU 服务器上，而把代理隔离在纯 CPU 沙箱中。每个用户似乎拥有一个私有且持久的沙箱，每个沙箱配备两个专用核心和 8GB 内存。按粗略估算，若采用双路 EPYC 9D25 系统，最多可提供 512 个 vCPU 和 2TB 内存，那么单个服务器托盘或节点可承载约 256 个 Muse 用户。以 50 万日活计算，大约需要 2000 个双路 EPYC 9D25、2TB 内存的服务器托盘。这个数字只是“餐巾纸数学”，Meta 可能混合使用多种 CPU-only 服务器，也可能存在配置开销；Turin 芯片本身支持高密度 DIMM，最高可达 6TB 内存。EPYC 在此类场景受欢迎，主要因为核心密度高——即使每个沙箱只分两个核心，乘以数十万甚至数百万用户后，CPU 总量仍然非常可观。

从技术架构看，Muse 体现了一种“推理与执行分离”的设计：GPU 集群负责大模型推理，CPU 集群负责运行用户专属沙箱、执行命令和维护持久状态。这样做可能有利于资源隔离、降低成本，并让 CPU 资源按用户规模横向扩展。AMD EPYC Turin 的高核心密度和内存扩展能力，使其适合承载大量轻量级、多租户的 AI 代理沙箱。但这一架构也把安全边界推到前台。

安全方面，Muse 并非完全开放。Hoffman 举例称，当 Muse 尝试查询内核缓冲区时，命令因权限不足而失败；sudo 等管理员命令预计也会被阻止。然而，Muse 似乎能够执行一些可能不安全的命令，Hoffman 甚至称 Muse 提出可以设置 SSH 连接到其私有 VM，并索要公钥。如果攻击者利用反向 SSH 隧道——由目标机器主动发起连接从而绕过防火墙——可能执行更具破坏性的操作。目前尚未发生实际攻击，但安全研究人员认为，擅长黑客技术的人可能借此获得可乘之机。

总体而言，这一事件揭示了大规模个人 AI 代理对 CPU 和内存的巨大需求，以及 Meta 在 Muse 上采用 AMD EPYC Turin、纯 CPU 沙箱与独立 GPU 推理集群解耦的工程选择。它同时提醒业界：当 AI 代理具备命令执行和工具调用能力时，沙箱隔离、权限控制、网络策略和命令审计必须成为核心设计，否则用户规模越大，潜在攻击面也越大。

history.title: Noctua explores 2,000W micro-channel air cooling
history.description: Noctua and Forced Physics are exploring whether densely packed micro-channels can provide extreme cooling performance without the noise associated with high-pressure airflow
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Noctua is teaming up with Forced Physics DCT to explore whether the company’s JouleForce micro-channel array-based cooling can be adapted for desktop PCs and workstations. The long–term partnership will focus on developing a quieter way to use the tech, although Noctua said in its announcement that the partnership is not tied to any specific product or release date.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs (Image credit: Noctua)Desktop GPU RoadmapNvidia's Enterprise GPU RoadmapTesting DirectStorage with GPU decompressionThe GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?Rubin in-depthThe Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PCClaimed to be a new third path to cooling, JouleForce goes beyond traditional air and liquid cooling methods. While it is still based on air-cooling, its capabilities far exceed today’s modern CPU coolers, with the ability to cool over 2000W of thermal energy. The technology uses densely packed micro-channels designed to improve heat transfer. According to Forced Physics, its geometry prevents the boundary layer that normally forms along cooling surfaces, allowing heat to be extracted along the entire length of each channel. This essentially enables large amounts of heat to be removed using air alone, without requiring a liquid-cooling loop.While that sounds impressive, bringing the technology to desktop PCs comes with a major challenge. The micro-channel arrays currently have a pressure drop that is “an order of magnitude and more” above the range of conventional PC fans. Thus, in its current state, JouleForce relies on industrial blowers, high-speed centrifugal fans, or even vacuum pumps to push air through the arrays.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Noctua’s expertise could prove useful as the company is known for developing some of the best performing PC fans. The partnership will investigate ways to reduce the pressure required by the micro-channel arrays or generate the necessary static pressure without making desktop systems excessively loud. “The pressure levels this technology requires in today’s implementations are currently supplied by equipment nobody would want on or under their desk, so this is a demanding, long-term engineering task – and one that we are eager to tackle,” said Roland Mossig, CEO at Noctua.For now, Noctua and Forced Physics are still in the early research stage, with both companies planning to share updates as the project reaches significant milestones. If the two companies can crack the airflow and acoustic challenges, JouleForce could eventually make its way to desktop PCs. At the same time, Noctua would have a serious advantage in the market compared to other heatsink manufacturers. history.descriptionZh:
Noctua 宣布与 Forced Physics DCT 合作，探索将其基于 JouleForce 微通道阵列的冷却技术适配到桌面 PC 和工作站。双方建立的是长期合作伙伴关系，重点研究如何让这项技术在桌面环境中以更安静的方式运行。不过 Noctua 在公告中明确表示，该合作目前并不绑定任何具体产品或发布时间。

这项合作的技术背景在于，桌面 CPU 和 GPU 的功耗持续上升，传统风冷散热器在性能、噪音和体积上面临越来越大的压力，而水冷虽然性能更强，却可能带来水泵噪音、漏液风险和安装复杂度等问题。JouleForce 被宣传为继传统风冷和水冷之后的“第三条散热路径”。它本质上仍属于风冷，但能力远超当今主流 CPU 散热器，可处理超过 2000W 的热能。

JouleForce 的核心是密集排列的微通道阵列，用来提升热传递效率。按照 Forced Physics 的说法，其特殊几何结构能够阻止冷却表面通常会形成的边界层，使空气可以沿每个微通道的整个长度带走热量。传统散热器中，边界层会形成一层近乎停滞的空气，像隔热层一样限制散热；而 JouleForce 的设计试图消除这一限制，从而仅靠空气就能移除大量热量，不需要液冷回路。

但要把这项技术带入桌面 PC，最大挑战在于气流压力。当前微通道阵列的压降比传统 PC 风扇所能提供的范围高出“一个数量级甚至更多”。因此，在现阶段，JouleForce 依赖工业鼓风机、高速离心风扇，甚至真空泵来推动空气穿过微通道阵列。这些设备显然不适合普通桌面或办公环境。

Noctua 的专长正好可能派上用场。该公司以开发高性能、低噪音 PC 风扇著称。合作将研究两条路径：一是降低微通道阵列所需的压力，二是设法在不让桌面系统变得过于吵闹的前提下产生必要静压。Noctua 首席执行官 Roland Mossig 表示，目前这项技术所需的压力水平只能由“没人愿意放在桌下或桌上的设备”提供，因此这是一个要求很高的长期工程任务，但 Noctua 乐于迎接挑战。

目前，Noctua 和 Forced Physics 仍处于早期研究阶段，双方计划在项目达到重要里程碑时分享进展。如果两家公司能够解决气流和声学难题，JouleForce 最终可能进入桌面 PC 市场，而 Noctua 也将相比其他散热器制造商获得显著优势。从应用前景看，这项技术有望为高功耗 CPU、GPU 和工作站提供一种高密度、无需液冷且更安静的高性能散热方案，但距离真正商用仍有很长的路要走。
