history.content: A few years back, I was at a beachside Easter egg hunt, watching my kids dash through sand dunes searching for sweet treats. My phone buzzed in my pocket; I ignored it. A moment later, it buzzed again. I pulled it out, glanced down, and saw a “motion detected” notification from my security camera. “Just my dog in the yard,” I thought, dismissing it.As the colorful eggs piled up in the baskets, my phone kept buzzing. Reluctantly, I pulled it out again and saw several more “motion detected” alerts. I tried to load a video clip, but it just buffered endlessly.AI-powered text descriptions paint the whole scene in a sentence. When I returned home, I found my four pet chickens dead, killed by my small border terrier. Looking back over the camera footage, I saw that they had pushed open their coop door, which I, in a rush to get to the Easter festivities, hadn’t properly secured.If instead of “motion detected,” that first notification had read “small dog chasing a chicken,” I would have raced back home and maybe saved them.Today, that type of notification is possible. With AI-generated text descriptions, a short message describing what the camera saw can arrive almost instantly, well before a video feed loads, painting the whole scene in a sentence.RelatedApple’s smart home camera service is starting to impress meWhy Apple’s next computer should be for the smart homeI let Gemini watch my family for the weekend — it got weirdMost major security camera companies now offer text descriptions, which combine traditional motion triggers with Vision Language Models, including Ring, Google Nest, Blink, Wyze, and Arlo. This month, with iOS 27, Apple finally brought the capability to its HomeKit Secure Video service with the launch of Apple Intelligence for Home.The surprise is that Apple is charging up to three times as much as its competition for the feature. Is it worth it? And are security cameras getting better at telling us about what actually matters?You’d think no one can get past my door without me knowing about it.I’ve been testing Apple Intelligence for Home since it launched in beta this summer, alongside Amazon Ring’s and Google Nest’s AI camera features introduced last year. I installed several cameras for each, but for this piece, I focused mainly on video doorbells — which I set up when iOS 27 officially arrived on September 14th. I tested a Ring Wired Doorbell Pro ($249.99), Google Nest Doorbell 2K ($199.99), and for Apple, the HomeKit Secure Video-compatible Aqara Doorbell Camera G400 ($99).I focused on how quickly each service sent the AI-powered notifications, how accurate and useful the descriptions were at telling me what happened, and how reliably it captured and notified me about activity. I also tested other AI-powered features each platform offers, including Apple’s ability to search and stitch together activity across multiple cameras, Ring’s Unusual Event that distinguished normal activity from out-of-the-ordinary events, and Google’s ability to trigger automations based on what a camera sees.The AI features on all three platforms are a significant improvement over their basic smart alerts. It’s now easier to understand what’s happening at a glance and decide whether to react, and security cameras feel more useful and less annoying overall.Ultimately, the real value of AI in cameras isn’t in describing what they see, but in using that knowledge to figure out what you actually need to know, and eventually what your home should do about it.What Apple Intelligence provides, at what priceHow to use Apple Intelligence for HomeYou need an iCloud Plus plan, a HomeKit Secure Video-compatible camera, an Apple Home Hub running HomePod/tvOS 27, and an AI-capable iPhone running iOS 27. Three iCloud Plus tiers support Apple Intelligence on one or more cameras:2TB plan: $9.99 a month (or Apple One / $39.95 a month) for one camera6TB plan: $29.99 a month for two cameras12TB plan: $59.99 a month for up to five camerasNo tier supports more than five cameras.Note: standard HomeKit Secure Video recording also requires an iCloud Plus plan, starting at $0.99 for one camera (50GB plan), $2.99 for five (200GB), and $9.99 for unlimited (2TB). All tiers that include Apple Intelligence support basic HKSV features on unlimited cameras.Apple Intelligence is on by default for Reduce Notifications and off by default for Summarize Videos. To adjust, go to Settings in the Home app, scroll down to Apple Intelligence, toggle on Summarize Video, and select participating cameras.With Apple Intelligence, a compatible camera connected to Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video service can send you text descriptions through the Apple Home app: “A dog sat on the floor,” “a cat played in the room,” “someone delivered a package.”It also enables natural-language video search, surfaces “noteworthy” events, stitches relevant clips together, and adds a reduce notifications feature that combines related events into a single alert that updates. This is in addition to the existing smart alerts, facial recognition, and 10 days of video storage available with HomeKit Secure Video.Pricing is where it gets tricky. Apple Intelligence for Home is bundled into iCloud Plus: $10 a month covers one camera, $30 covers two, and $60 up to five (see sidebar). No tier supports more than five cameras.By comparison, Google Home’s Nest cameras offer Gemini-powered text descriptions, video search, facial recognition, and a daily Home Brief digest — which summarizes the day’s activity in a short paragraph (sometimes with a fictional slant) — for $20 a month, covering unlimited cameras and 24/7 recording on wired models.Amazon’s Ring also charges $20 a month for its AI text descriptions, video search, facial recognition, unusual events alerts, and clip recording on unlimited cameras, with 24/7 costing an extra $3 per camera on wired models. Ring has its own reduced notification option that rolls similar events from the same camera into one notification, such as “Brian is mowing the lawn.”Apple says the leastText descriptions are a game changer for security cameras. For me, getting an alert that says “A FedEx delivery person is walking on the lawn” rather than “person detected at front door” is the difference between getting up and going downstairs or carrying on working. But quality and accuracy vary wildly, even within a single provider.Sometimes I get useful details, other times a few words that tell me almost nothing. Then there were the times when the descriptions were detailed, but laughably wrong: “A tennis serve simulator is rolling on the walkway,” “A gray hoverboard is driving on the pathway” — both misidentifications of a robot lawn mower.PreviousNext1/3I donned a Ghostface mask to see how the various AIs would react. Nest sent the most useful alert.In my testing, text alerts from Google and Ring provided the most context and specificity, and Apple often didn’t try, saying “someone” rather than providing any detail. For example, it would say “someone is walking in the yard,” whereas Ring and Google provided more context: a delivery person is walking in the yard, a person in uniform, someone carrying a bag, and so on.Apple was also the briefest. For example, when my cat was on the front porch, Apple said, “A cat sat on the porch.” Ring went with “A cat is standing on the pathway outside the porch.” Google Home told me which cat: “A black and white cat walks across the porch.”All three identified delivery trucks, correctly flagging UPS and FedEx vehicles driving past, as well as delivery people approaching the door. Apple was the only one to ID the USPS van pulling up to my mailbox, although not consistently.Google was the most descriptive with vehicles — “a light-colored car drives by on the street” or “a white van,” “a dark-colored SUV” — Apple and Ring mostly said “a vehicle drove by,” sometimes with a type (van, car, truck).Apple’s reduce notifications feature combines several alerts into one.These were difficult to read and not terribly useful.Apple’s descriptions were the hardest to digest at a glance, particularly the combined ones through reduce notifications. For example, “Someone seen. Someone carried a box” is clunky. Ring and Google merge the events more fluidly into “a person carried a box up the driveway.”In fairness, Apple Intelligence in Home only officially launched this month, so I expect this to improve, but as things stand, Ring’s and Google’s are more useful and cost less.Finicky facial recognition and alertsFor a doorbell camera, the real advantage of AI descriptions is knowing who’s there right away. All three offer facial recognition alongside the ability to spot a UPS driver or similar.Ring was the most consistently accurate, identifying me every time I approached the door. Apple hedged its bets, sometimes identifying me, sometimes saying “Someone who may be Jennifer Pattison Tuohy,” and other times just “Someone.” Google got it right about half the time; the other half it thought I was my daughter’s best mate (a change from the UPS driver it pegged me as for most of last year).Apple just wasn’t sure about me.Ring was the most accurate; Google was mostly accurate.Text descriptions are more useful if they show up, and quickly. But on the doorbell camera I was testing, Apple’s often didn’t. Apple Home reliably alerted me when someone pressed the doorbell, and it recorded every event, but notifications about other motion events were inconsistent.A potential issue here is that, unlike its competition, Apple doesn’t control the whole experience. HomeKit Secure Video only works with third-party hardware — there are no Apple cameras yet. I was using the G400, Aqara’s latest wired doorbell camera.When I first set it up, alerts arrived in Apple Home with no issues, but at some point they stopped, and no amount of troubleshooting brought them back. However, alerts kept coming through in the Aqara app. I also still got doorbell ring alerts in the Home app, and notifications from other Aqara cameras continued to work.The Google Nest doorbell captured everything and was consistently first to notify me of an event. Ring was also fast and mostly reliable; its notifications showed up just after Google’s, though I’d occasionally get “This video is unavailable” when trying to play back footage.Reliability is Apple’s biggest fix, plus some innovationThe good news is that recording in HomeKit Secure Video has improved significantly with iOS 27. Apple said it completely rearchitected the system, which addresses a long-standing problem with missing clips.I’ve noticed that cameras load faster, are more stable, and no longer miss recordings. An Eve outdoor camera that was almost always offline has been stable since the upgrade, and the Aqara Camera Hub G5 outdoor camera and G350 indoor camera have also been solid. The G400 doorbell camera has been the only problem child, with missing notifications, but it records consistently.All the other HomeKit cameras I tested reliably sent alerts; only the Aqara doorbell camera had the issue, but even when I didn’t get alerts, I could use video search to find events.Typing “When did the USPS truck come” in the Apple Home app pulled up every instance the Aqara doorbell spotted the mail delivery. In comparison, while the Nest Cam didn’t identify the USPS truck as often, its video search results contained more specifics, including an event where the mail person dropped off an Amazon package.Of the three, Google’s video search was the most useful, followed by Ring’s, then Apple’s, which directly correlates with the amount of detail each provides in the text descriptions.Apple has two features Ring and Google don’t offer. The first is clip stitching, where Apple Intelligence identifies someone or something on one camera, recognizes it again on another, understands these are related, and plays the sequence as a single video in the Home app. I haven’t found a real use for this so far, but it’s been fun for tracking my dog around the house when I’m out.The second feature is bringing events that Apple judges important to the top of the search box. In the last two weeks, it’s only highlighted the trash pickup ━ I guess my life just isn’t that noteworthy.Here’s where Ring winsOne of the biggest problems with security cameras is filtering out the important info from the sheer volume of everything they see. Even with AI notifications turned on, I still get a stream of alerts from Apple Home and Google Home. Some are more useful than they used to be, but overload is still an issue.These are the only alerts Ring sent from the doorbell camera over an entire weekend when I had Unusual Event enabled.Apple’s noteworthy events is a similar concept, but it doesn’t send a specific alert instead just surfacing the clip to the top of your search page.While Apple’s noteworthy events feature shows promise, Ring’s Unusual Event feature is the best solution I’ve seen. It learns what normal traffic looks like for each camera, then notifies you only when something isn’t normal. This summer, I cut my Ring notifications down from around 40 a day to just two or three.Instead of getting an alert every time my cat is on my porch, I only get one when a raccoon or possum walks by. It doesn’t send alerts when my son comes home from school, but it does when he comes home at 2AM. The camera by my chicken coop no longer sends a series of notifications when someone is feeding them or collecting eggs — but it does alert me when I am out there at midnight with a flashlight to wrestle a snake.What’s next: cameras that can actThe cats were a big fan of Google Home’s inability to tell them apart, as it meant more kibble. (This is not Smokey).The natural progression here is automations triggered by the camera understanding what it sees. Turn on the sprinklers if there’s a raccoon in the backyard, but not if it’s just my dog. A cat at the back door broadcasts an alert through my smart speakers so someone can let them in. The trash truck rolling past without stopping sends an urgent notification to put the bins out before it comes back the other way.This is where cameras move beyond being simply security devices to become intelligent smart-home sensors that can understand what’s happening and potentially act on it.Google Home recently added the ability to trigger automations from camera alerts, although in my early testing, it’s not reliable enough.I tried it with my three cats and a pet feeder using Google’s new Pet Memory feature. But instead of only dispensing food for one specific cat as I asked, it triggered every time it saw a cat. At least the cats were happy.The problem is accuracy. When AI can’t reliably identify the subject, the automations can’t respond reliably. So, my earlier example of Apple accurately recognizing the USPS van half the time would mean any automation I set up to alert me the mail is here would only work half the time.Today, Apple doesn’t have this capability, but if the rumors that the company is developing its own video doorbell and security camera are true, I would expect to see a feature like this come to Apple Home.The privacy tradeoffThe smarter cameras become, the more they need to know about your home. For a system to understand what’s normal, it needs to learn who lives there, when they come and go, which pets are around, and which vehicles belong. This raises very real concerns around privacy and surveillance.Ring has faced particular scrutiny over its cloud-based architecture and partnerships with law enforcement. Where Google and Apple can start with local processing, Ring processes all footage in the cloud by default.There’s real benefit in a system knowing everything about my home — I’d just prefer to be the only one who knows it.Last month, Ring announced an overhaul to that model, introducing a new default encryption system called TAKE. This rotates encryption keys for cloud-stored video and deletes Ring’s copy after 24 hours. Among other privacy protections, including no admin access, Ring says this means it can no longer hand over decrypted footage to the police. However, it can still be compelled to provide encrypted files.With Apple’s standard HomeKit Secure Video, your home hub processes footage locally and encrypts it end-to-end before sending it to the cloud for storage. But adding Apple Intelligence changes that: Video summaries are now processed in the cloud using Apple’s Private Cloud Compute (PCC), where they are unencrypted for processing.According to Apple, PCC writes the captions, sends them back, and then “permanently deletes the data from PCC.” Apple support docs also state that there is no admin access, and nothing identifies who the footage belongs to.RelatedOur picks for the best privacy-focused video doorbellsThe best smart doorbell camerasCameras get an Apple Intelligence boost in Apple HomeGoogle takes a similar approach to Apple, but without end-to-end encryption; footage is encrypted in transit and at rest. Gemini for Home-enabled Nest cameras can use some on-device processing, but the heavy work is done in the Gemini cloud, in line with Google Home’s privacy practices.A big question for me is whether all this intelligence has to live on someone else’s computers. There’s real benefit in a system knowing everything about my home — I’d just prefer to be the only one who knows it. For privacy, security, and potentially speed, local AI processing and storage feels like the right answer. Manufacturers including Anker Eufy, Reolink, Ubiquiti UniFi, and UGreen already have or have announced products that do this.With a new Apple TV, HomePod, and a possible smart display all rumored to be imminent, Apple’s next generation of hardware might shift more processing back into the house — which could mean paying less every month for the privilege.When Ghostface is at my door, I want Apple Home to tell me.Is Apple Intelligence worth it?Based on my testing of the beta and the initial full release, Apple Intelligence in Home has brought substantial improvements, finally putting HomeKit Secure Video in contention with Ring and Google.Whether it’s worth the price depends on how many cameras you own. If you have one — say, a video doorbell — Apple Intelligence is a reasonable deal at $10 a month if you also need 2TB of iCloud storage. You get competent descriptions, better video search, and Apple’s privacy position. Even with multiple cameras, you can get some benefit by enabling it on just one.Next let’s make them better at telling us what actually matters.However, if you want AI capabilities across your home, including clip stitching, the math gets bad fast. At five cameras, you’re paying $60 a month for Apple to tell you “a cat sat on the porch” or “a vehicle drove by.” The competition gives you more detailed descriptions on as many cameras as you own for $20 a month.Today, you’re paying an Apple premium for less. But this is Apple’s first move, and I expect it to improve. AI has unlocked genuine utility here, making security cameras better at telling us what’s happening; next, let’s make them better at telling us what actually matters.A few years ago, a “motion detected” alert wasn’t enough to tell me that my chickens were in trouble. Today, AI can tell me it’s a dog chasing a chicken. The next step is for it to understand that this is something I need to know right now and make sure I get that information quickly enough to act. Eventually, an intelligent home might actually be able to do something about it, too.That’s the smart home I want. But we’re not there yet.Photos and screenshots by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

history.descriptionZh:
几年前，作者在复活节捡蛋活动中收到安全摄像头“检测到运动”通知，未加理会，回家后发现四只宠物鸡被自家边境梗犬咬死。回看录像，鸡舍门被鸡推开，而他因匆忙未关好。如果第一条通知不是“检测到运动”，而是“小狗在追鸡”，他可能及时赶回救下鸡。这个亲身经历引出文章主题：AI 生成的文本描述正在改变安全摄像头，让通知从简单运动触发变成一句语义描述，并且几乎即时到达，远早于视频画面加载。

技术原理上，主流安防厂商 Ring、Google Nest、Blink、Wyze、Arlo 现在都提供文本描述，把传统运动触发与视觉语言模型结合。Apple 则在 iOS 27 中通过 Apple Intelligence for Home 将这一能力带入 HomeKit Secure Video。文章测试了 Apple、Ring、Google 三家的 AI 摄像头，主要聚焦视频门铃：Ring Wired Doorbell Pro（249.99 美元）、Google Nest Doorbell 2K（199.99 美元），以及 Apple 侧兼容 HomeKit Secure Video 的 Aqara Doorbell Camera G400（99 美元）。测试关注通知速度、描述准确性和有用性、事件捕获可靠性，也测试了跨摄像头搜索与拼接、异常事件、基于摄像头内容的自动化等功能。

Apple Intelligence 需要 iCloud+ 计划、兼容 HomeKit Secure Video 的摄像头、运行 HomePod/tvOS 27 的 Apple Home Hub，以及支持 AI 的 iPhone 和 iOS 27。功能包括文本描述、自然语言视频搜索、突出“值得注意”的事件、跨摄像头片段拼接，以及把相关事件合并为一条更新通知的“减少通知”。它默认开启减少通知，默认关闭视频摘要。价格方面，2TB iCloud+ 每月 9.99 美元支持一台摄像头，6TB 每月 29.99 美元支持两台，12TB 每月 59.99 美元最多支持五台；没有任何层级支持超过五台摄像头。标准 HomeKit Secure Video 录制另需 iCloud+，起价每月 0.99 美元支持一台 50GB，2.99 美元支持五台 200GB，9.99 美元支持无限 2TB；含 Apple Intelligence 的层级仍可在无限摄像头上使用基本 HomeKit Secure Video 功能。对比之下，Google Home 的 Nest 摄像头以每月 20 美元提供 Gemini 文本描述、视频搜索、面部识别、每日 Home Brief 摘要，覆盖无限摄像头，有线型号还可 24/7 录制。Ring 同样每月 20 美元，提供 AI 文本描述、视频搜索、面部识别、异常事件警报和无限摄像头剪辑录制，有线型号 24/7 录制每台另加 3 美元。Apple 在单摄像头时价格尚可，但多摄像头场景下最高五台 60 美元/月，而对手 20 美元即可覆盖无限摄像头，价格差距明显。

实际体验中，Google 和 Ring 的文本描述上下文最丰富、最具体，Apple 则往往最简短，常只说“某人”，而不提供更多细节。例如猫在前廊时，Apple 说“一只猫坐在门廊”，Ring 说“一只猫站在门廊外的小路上”，Google 则说“一只黑白猫走过门廊”。三者都能识别 UPS 和 FedEx 车辆及快递员，Apple 偶尔是唯一识别出 USPS 面包车开近邮箱的，但并不稳定；Google 对车辆描述最详细。Apple 的合并通知也较生硬，例如“有人被看到。有人拿着箱子”，而 Ring 和 Google 会合并成“一个人把箱子搬上车道”。面部识别方面，Ring 最一致准确，Google 约一半正确，Apple 有时识别出作者，有时说“可能是 Jennifer Pattison Tuohy”，有时只说“某人”。通知可靠性上，Google Nest 最快且捕获完整，Ring 也快且大多可靠，Apple 门铃按下时通知可靠，但其他运动事件通知不一致；Aqara G400 曾停止发送通知。不过 iOS 27 重构了 HomeKit Secure Video，录制稳定性显著改善，摄像头加载更快、不再漏录，其他 HomeKit 摄像头也较稳定。视频搜索中，Google 最有用，Ring 次之，Apple 第三，这与三者文本描述的详细程度直接相关。Apple 独有跨摄像头片段拼接和重要事件置顶，但作者认为实用性有限，后者过去两周只突出了垃圾回收。

Ring 的 Unusual Event 被作者视为最佳创新。它学习每台摄像头的正常活动，只在异常时通知。作者夏天把 Ring 通知从每天约 40 条降到 2 至 3 条：猫在门廊不再通知，浣熊或负鼠经过才通知；儿子放学回家不通知，凌晨 2 点回家则通知；鸡舍喂食或捡蛋不通知，但午夜拿手电筒抓蛇会通知。下一步自然是摄像头理解所见并触发自动化，例如后院有

history.title: Intel expects 14A to be 'within 5%' the performance of TSMC's A14
history.description: Intel's Naga Chandrasekaran now claims that Intel 14A node will deliver performance 'within 5%' of TSMC's A14 technology, a claim that requires a closer examination.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Intel's 14A (1.4nm-class) process technology is expected to deliver performance 'within 5%' of TSMC's A14 (1.4nm-class) production node, Naga Chandrasekaran, the chief technology and operations officer as well as general manager of Intel Foundry, told investment banking firm KeyBanc (via @Alex_Intel_). Given TSMC's track record of delivering steady performance, power, and area (PPA) gains with every new node, this might sound like entirely good news. However, the statement deserves a closer examination.Delivering 'within 5%' performance is an ambiguous statement that may mean that 14A will be 5% faster than A14, or that 14A will be 5% slower than A14. While 'within 5%' performance compared to the direct rival of the same class may sound like a good competitive position, in recent years Intel's process technologies trailed TSMC's nodes in transistor density and remained competitive in performance or power. This was, to a large degree, attributed to Intel's historic focus on CPU performance, but not necessarily transistor density, as its own fabs have offset additional costs associated with larger dies.In fact, actual shipping processors suggest Intel's 18A is at least competitive with TSMC's N2 in maximum achievable CPU frequency as Intel's Core Ultra X9 388H 'Panther Lake' can hit 5.10 GHz (at an 80W max turbo power), AMD's EPYC 9586F has the highest single-core clock of 5.0 GHz (at a default 500W CPU power), Apple's A20 Pro can achieve 4.93 GHz, whereas Apple's M6 can hit 4.78 GHz. These numbers should not be converted directly into a statement such as '18A is X% faster than N2,' because the processors use different architectures, voltages, standard-cell libraries, thermal envelopes, and physical implementations. However, they do provide a useful real-world reference point: the available N2 processors do not show a substantial frequency advantage over 18A. If anything, the highest observed CPU frequencies favor Intel's process.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Based on internal estimates, Intel officially states that compared to its already fast 18A, its 14A is expected to provide 15% – 20% higher performance at the same power, or 25% – 35% lower power at the same frequency and transistor count. By contrast, TSMC expects its A14 to be 10% - 15% faster than N2 at the same power, or 25% - 30% lower power at the same clocks and transistor count.Combining the observed 18A and N2 CPU frequencies of Intel's 18A and TSMC's N2 with Intel's stated 15% – 20% 14A gain and TSMC's assumed 10% – 15% A14 gain would ordinarily suggest a modest 14A performance advantage of A14 even in most conservative scenarios for Intel. Therefore, Intel's new expectation that 14A will be 'within 5%' of A14 is notably less ambitious than one might infer from the company's published process specifications, even though the 'within 5%' statement does not tell us which process Intel expects to lead. You may like TSMC confirms significant yield and performance improvements in A14 update Intel 14A defect density is dropping faster than the company expected SMIC's third-gen 7nm node shows smaller metal pitch than Intel 18A, higher transistor density than TSMC N6 without EUV In fact, advantages of Intel's 14A over TSMC's A14 can be calculated using the highest observed 18A and N2 CPU clocks combined with Intel's and TSMC's official iso power performance projections. Swipe to scroll horizontally Scenario Intel 14A gain vs. 18A TSMC A14 gain vs. N2 14A extrapolation from 5.10 GHz A14 extrapolation from 5.00 GHz Implied 14A advantage Intel worstTSMC best 15% 15% 5.865 5.75 2.00% Both minimum gains 15% 10% 5.865 5.5 6.60% Both maximum gains 20% 15% 6.12 5.75 6.40% Intel bestTSMC worst 20% 10% 6.12 5.5 11.30% Starting points: Intel 18A = 5.10 GHz (Core Ultra 9 388H); TSMC N2 = 5.00 GHz (EPYC 9586F).Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsWith Intel’s Core Ultra X9 388H and AMD’s EPYC 9586F as the starting points, the official iso-power performance projections imply a 2% – 11.3% potential performance advantage for 14A over A14, depending on the combination of process-performance assumptions. Swipe to scroll horizontally Scenario Intel 14A gain vs. 18A TSMC A14 gain vs. N2 14A extrapolation from 5.10 GHz A14 extrapolation from 4.788 GHz Implied 14A advantage Intel worstTSMC best 15% 15% 5.865 5.506 6.50% Both minimum gains 15% 10% 5.865 5.267 11.40% Both maximum gains 20% 15% 6.12 5.506 11.20% Intel bestTSMC worst 20% 10% 6.12 5.267 16.20% Starting points: Intel 18A = 5.10 GHz (Core Ultra 9 388H); TSMC N2 = 4.78 GHz (Apple M6).Using Apple's M6 as the real-world N2 reference, a similar calculation gives Intel 14A a 6.5% – 16.2% implied advantage over TSMC A14. Even the worst possible combination for Intel — 14A achieves only +15% while A14 achieves the full +15% — puts Intel's node well beyond the 'within 5%' estimate given by Naga Chandrasekaran.It should be clearly noted that our calculations do not predict 14A or A14 CPU frequencies, as we use clocks from current CPU architectures with improvement claims for upcoming process technologies. The calculation is useful primarily for illustrating what the companies' published numbers imply relative to today's products.Intel's 'within 5%' assessment raises an interesting question: why does Intel expect 14A and A14 to be so close when the companies' published process gains appear to suggest a larger gap? Perhaps Intel's assessment incorporates factors that these simple calculations do not capture. Or perhaps the head of Intel Foundry took a page from his boss Lip-Bu Tan's book and now prefers to underpromise. history.titleZh: Intel expects 14A to be 'within 5%' the performance of TSMC's A14
history.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware 报道，Intel Foundry 首席技术与运营官兼总经理 Naga Chandrasekaran 向投资银行 KeyBanc 表示，Intel 的 14A（1.4nm 级）工艺预计性能将落在台积电 A14（1.4nm 级）的“5%以内”。这句话看似说明 Intel 已接近台积电下一代节点，但表述本身有歧义：14A 可能比 A14 快 5%，也可能慢 5%。考虑到台积电历来能在每代节点上稳定交付性能、功耗和面积（PPA）提升，这一说法值得进一步审视。

背景方面，近年来 Intel 工艺在晶体管密度上落后于台积电，但在性能或功耗上仍保持竞争力。文章认为，这在很大程度上源于 Intel 历史上更关注 CPU 性能而非晶体管密度，同时 Intel 自有晶圆厂可以抵消较大芯片面积带来的额外成本。实际出货处理器也显示，Intel 18A 至少在最高 CPU 频率上与台积电 N2 有竞争力：Intel Core Ultra X9 388H“Panther Lake”可在 80W 最大加速功耗下达到 5.10 GHz；AMD EPYC 9586F 在默认 500W 下达到 5.0 GHz 单核最高频率；Apple A20 Pro 可达 4.93 GHz，Apple M6 可达 4.78 GHz。文章强调，不能把这些数字直接换算成“18A 比 N2 快 X%”，因为不同处理器采用不同架构、电压、标准单元库、热设计功耗和物理实现。但它们提供了现实参考：现有 N2 处理器并未显示出明显频率优势，最高观测频率反而对 Intel 工艺有利。

根据 Intel 内部估计，14A 相比已经较快的 18A，可在相同功耗下提升 15%–20% 性能，或在相同频率和晶体管数量下降低 25%–35% 功耗。台积电则预计 A14 在相同功耗下比 N2 快 10%–15%，或在相同频率和晶体管数量下降低 25%–30% 功耗。若把当前 18A 和 N2 处理器的最高频率，与两家公司公布的等功耗性能提升幅度结合推算，通常会得出 14A 相对 A14 有一定优势，即使采用对 Intel 最保守的假设也是如此。因此，Intel 现在称 14A 将在 A14 的“5%以内”，比从其公布工艺规格中可推断出的预期要保守得多，尽管“5%以内”并未说明 Intel 预计谁领先。

文章用两组起点进行了推算。第一组以 Intel 18A = 5.10 GHz（Core Ultra 9 388H）、台积电 N2 = 5.00 GHz（EPYC 9586F）为起点：在“Intel 最差、台积电最好”的场景下，即 14A 比 18A 提升 15%、A14 比 N2 提升 15%，14A 推算频率为 5.865 GHz，A14 为 5.75 GHz，隐含 14A 领先约 2.0%；在双方都取最小提升时领先约 6.6%；双方都取最大提升时领先约 6.4%；在“Intel 最好、台积电最差”时领先约 11.3%。因此，按官方等功耗性能预测，14A 对 A14 的潜在性能优势约为 2%–11.3%，具体取决于假设组合。

第二组以 Apple M6 的 4.788 GHz 作为 N2 现实参考：在 Intel 最差、台积电最好场景下，14A 对 A14 隐含优势约 6.5%；双方最小提升时约 11.4%；双方最大提升时约 11.2%；Intel 最好、台积电最差时约 16.2%。也就是说，若用 Apple M6 作为 N2 参考，Intel 14A 对台积电 A14 的隐含优势可达 6.5%–16.2%。即便采用对 Intel 最不利的组合——14A 仅提升 15%，而 A14 达到完整 15% 提升——Intel 节点仍然超出 Chandrasekaran 所说的“5%以内”。

文章同时明确，这些计算并不是在预测 14A 或 A14 的实际 CPU 频率，而是用当前 CPU 架构的频率，加上两家公司对即将到来的工艺技术的改进声明，来展示其公布数字相对当今产品意味着什么。Intel 的“5%以内”评估引出一个问题：为什么 Intel 预计 14A 和 A14 会如此接近，而两家公司公布的工艺增益似乎暗示更大差距？一种可能是 Intel 的评估纳入了这些简单计算未捕捉的因素；另一种可能是，Intel Foundry 负责人借鉴其上司陈立武（Lip-Bu Tan）的风格，如今更倾向于少承诺、留余地。总体而言，14A 是 Intel Foundry 与台积电 A14 竞争的关键节点；若真能落在 A14 的 5%以内，将意味着 Intel 回到与台积电同一梯队，但按公开规格推算，14A 的潜力可能被低估，最终仍需实际产品验证。

history.title: New Jersey hits Microsoft-linked AI data center with record fine for 62 unpermitted power generators, issues 45-day shutdown deadline
history.description: The DataOne data center is facing a record fine of $1.07 million for operating portable turbine generators without permission. Residents say that the penalty is a drop in the bucket for these big tech companies.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The DataOne data center in Vineland, New Jersey, has just been hit with a record $1.07 million fine for operating unpermitted portable generators on the construction site. According to the New York Times, state inspectors spotted 62 of these units powering the facility back in late July.Residents had already complained about it at a February town hall meeting. Inspectors said that there were no generators on site when they first visited in December last year. However, some residents said that “some type of unit” was spotted by satellite imagery back in February, leading to their complaint at the community assembly.Residents of Vineland have already made multiple complaints about the development. Some of the issues t include the unpermitted construction of a 1.5-million-gallon LNG tank and unacceptable noise levels, especially at night, that affected homes within a half-mile radius of the construction site. They also said that there was little to no public consultation on the project before it went into full swing, with the people only finding out that a data center was being constructed in their neighborhood after Microsoft announced a $33 billion deal with Nebius, which in turn contracted DataOne to supply the compute they need.Despite a record fine, some residents feel that the punishment isn’t enough. “It’s a ‘don’t ask for permission, just ask for forgiveness later’ kind of deal,” longtime Vineland resident Steve Brown told the Times. He also added, “It’s still kind of a drop in the bucket for a company that has several billion dollars of capital.” Long-time community member Tiffany Leone-Vespa also added, “What’s $1.07 million? They should have done it for each generator they were running illegally. They’re billionaires. It’s like pocket change.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: On the other hand, DataOne disagreed with the fine. A company spokesperson said that “We will apply for the air permits for the temporary generators,” and also added that it’s transitioning from the polluting and noisy portable turbines to more modern fuel cells. New Jersey ordered it to comply with the permitting requirements and to stop using the generators if they’re not granted within 45 days.This is a similar situation that the citizens of Memphis and Southaven faced when SpaceXAI deployed 69 unpermitted generators to provide power to its Colossus 2 data center. It has become the subject of a lawsuit, especially as the community raised concerns that they were spewing thousands of tons of pollutants in the primarily black neighborhood. However, the Department of Justice stepped in and asked the court to dismiss the case because the site “supports mission-critical operations.” Elon Musk’s company eventually agreed to remove all unpermitted turbines, but said that the process will take over a year as replacement 1.2-gigawatt plants gradually come online. history.titleZh: 新泽西州对与微软有关联的AI数据中心开出创纪录罚单，因其62台未经许可的发电机，并下达45天关闭期限
history.descriptionZh:
新泽西州 Vineland 的 DataOne 数据中心因在建设现场运行 62 台未获许可的便携式发电机，被州监管机构开出创纪录的 107 万美元罚单。这一事件把 AI 数据中心高速扩张与地方环境、噪音、许可审批和社区知情权之间的矛盾推到了台前。背景是微软与 Nebius 达成 330 亿美元算力协议，Nebius 又委托 DataOne 提供所需算力；但当地居民表示，他们直到相关交易公布后，才发现社区附近正在建设数据中心，事前几乎没有公众咨询。

时间线显示，州检查员称去年 12 月首次到访时现场还没有发电机，但居民称今年 2 月卫星图像中已能看到“某种设备”，并在 2 月的镇民大会上提出投诉。到 7 月底，检查员发现共有 62 台便携式发电机在为该设施供电。居民此前还投诉该项目未经许可建设 150 万加仑的液化天然气储罐，以及尤其夜间不可接受的噪音，影响范围达到施工现场半英里半径内的住宅。液化天然气储罐用于把天然气冷却液化后储存，体积可缩小约 600 倍，便于运输和现场供气，但涉及易燃物安全和空气排放许可，不能随意建设。

从技术原理看，AI 数据中心需要数百兆瓦甚至吉瓦级的连续电力，而电网接入、变电站建设和排放许可往往需要较长时间。便携式燃气发电机或燃气轮机可以模块化、快速部署，通过燃烧天然气驱动涡轮或活塞发电，满足建设期或临时算力上线的电力缺口。但燃烧过程会产生氮氧化物、颗粒物、一氧化碳和二氧化碳，并伴随较大噪音。DataOne 表示不同意罚款，将申请临时发电机的空气许可，并称正从污染和噪音较大的便携式涡轮转向更现代的燃料电池。燃料电池通过电化学反应将燃料化学能直接转化为电能，不经过燃烧，因此氮氧化物和颗粒物排放更低、噪音更小、效率也较高；若使用天然气，仍会有二氧化碳排放，且需要燃料供应、水管理和空气许可，但相比便携式燃气机组是更清洁的分布式供电路线。

罚款数字本身也引发争议。107 万美元分摊到 62 台发电机，约合每台 1.73 万美元。居民 Steve Brown 称这是“先不申请许可，之后再求原谅”的做法，并认为对拥有数十亿美元资本的公司来说仍是九牛一毛。Tiffany Leone-Vespa 更直言：“107 万美元算什么？应该按每台非法运行的发电机来罚。他们是亿万富翁，这就像零钱。”新泽西州已命令 DataOne 在 45 天内满足许可要求，否则必须停止使用这些发电机。

类似冲突也出现在孟菲斯和 Southaven。马斯克旗下公司——原文称 SpaceXAI，通常指 xAI——曾为 Colossus 2 数据中心部署 69 台未获许可的发电机，引发诉讼，社区担心这些设备向以黑人为主的社区排放数千吨污染物。美国司法部后来介入，以该站点“支持关键任务运营”为由请求法院驳回案件。该公司最终同意移除所有未许可涡轮，但表示替换的 1.2 吉瓦发电厂逐步上线需要一年以上。相关报道还显示，威斯康星州居民也因噪音对微软相关 AI 数据中心提起集体诉讼，说明超大规模 AI 算力设施与周边社区的摩擦正在增多。

总体来看，这一事件的核心不只是罚款，而是 AI 算力竞赛下的电力瓶颈与监管滞后。为了快速上线 GPU 集群，数据中心开发商可能倾向使用现场燃气发电和液化天然气设施，绕过漫长电网排队和审批；但这类方案把排放、噪音和安全外部性转嫁给附近居民，并容易引发环境正义和诉讼风险。DataOne 转向燃料电池、新泽西设定 45 天合规期限，以及 Colossus 2 用 1.2 吉瓦电厂替换未许可涡轮，都表明行业正在被迫从“先部署、后补票”转向更合规的供电方案。未来，AI 数据中心的竞争力不仅取决于芯片和算力，也取决于能否在电网升级、储能、燃料电池、清洁发电和社区沟通之间找到可被监管与公众接受的平衡。

history.title: Google's orbital AI data center test packs four TPUs and 1,000W of solar power
history.description: Google will launch an experimental satellite into orbit on October 1, taking four tensor processing units with it.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Google is set to launch an experimental satellite, named MVP, into orbit next week to test running an AI data center in space. As part of a wider initiative called Project Suncatcher, the satellite will be aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket when it launches from the Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. Once in space, and assuming everything goes well, the tech on board the satellite will be capable of handling simple AI requests from space.The New York Times points out that while the move is an important one, the satellite will be limited in terms of its processing power. It will feature just four Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) and be similar to a single Earth-bound server in terms of capabilities. It will be powered by solar panels capable of providing a single kilowatt of power to the tensor chips.While clearly limited, the orbiting server is set to handle AI requests for up to a year, although it will remain in orbit for up to six years. After that, gravity will take hold, and the satellite will burn up during re-entry into Earth's atmosphere.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Before that happens, James Manyika, Google's senior vice president of research, expects to learn more about how space may become a home for future data centers, though probably not for a long time.“We don’t expect, to be perfectly frank, that we’ll have anything usefully operational in the next few years,” the SVP told the Times. He went on to compare the venture to Google's driverless cars, saying that Google was testing those "like 15 years before anything showed up." The idea of users accessing a version of Gemini running in space is some way from coming to fruition. Alongside Google, Elon Musk (xAI, Tesla, SpaceX), as well as Jeff Bezos (Amazon) and Sam Altman (OpenAI), have been making noises about the prospect of orbital data centers for some time now. China has already put its own AI compute into orbit. Even Intel has a patent for orbital data centers of its own.Putting servers into space does have its issues, not least the problem of getting them there. Radiation and computers don't get along, and the radiation found in space can cause "bit flips" that change the way chips process data. Google's answer, for now, is to restart the chips every so often to reset them. They'll only be able to run for around 15 minutes before they need to be shut down to allow them to cool off.Regardless, it's still early days for the concept of running servers in space. Google plans to launch a pair of satellites next, with long-term plans for networked fleets of more than 80 satellites also already floated.By Manyika's estimation, Google has 15 years to go from a four-chip server to a full-on data center. history.titleZh: 谷歌轨道AI数据中心测试：搭载四个TPU和1000瓦太阳能供电
history.descriptionZh:
谷歌计划在下周发射一颗名为 MVP 的实验卫星，作为“Project Suncatcher”计划的一部分，测试在太空中运行 AI 数据中心。该卫星将搭乘 SpaceX 的 Falcon 9 火箭，从加州范登堡太空军基地升空。如果一切顺利，星上技术将能够从太空处理简单的 AI 请求。不过《纽约时报》指出，这颗卫星的处理能力有限：它仅搭载四个张量处理单元（TPU），整体能力大致相当于地球上的一台服务器，由可提供 1 千瓦功率的太阳能板供电。该轨道服务器将处理 AI 请求最长约一年，但会在轨停留最长六年，之后受重力影响再入地球大气层并烧毁。

技术挑战方面，太空辐射会导致“位翻转”，改变芯片处理数据的方式；谷歌目前的应对办法是定期重启芯片以进行重置。冷却方面，由于太空中没有空气，传统风扇散热无法工作，谷歌设计了直接将热量排放到太空的冷却系统。但即便如此，四颗芯片仍会很快过热，只能运行约 15 分钟，就需要关机冷却。这些限制表明，太空 AI 服务器仍处于非常早期的实验阶段。

谷歌研究高级副总裁 James Manyika 表示，坦率地说，不指望未来几年内会有真正有实用价值的系统投入运行。他将这一尝试比作谷歌的无人驾驶汽车项目：谷歌在相关技术真正出现前约 15 年就开始测试。用户访问运行在太空中的 Gemini 版本，距离实现仍很遥远。不过，谷歌和其他公司预计会继续探索轨道数据中心。马斯克旗下的 xAI、Tesla、SpaceX，以及贝索斯的 Amazon 和奥特曼的 OpenAI，都曾提出类似设想；中国也已将自己的 AI 算力送入轨道，Intel 则拥有轨道数据中心相关专利。

按照谷歌的规划，下一步将发射两颗卫星，长期目标则是建立由超过 80 颗卫星组成的联网舰队。Manyika 估计，从目前的四芯片服务器发展到完整数据中心，大约还需要 15 年。总体来看，这次 MVP 卫星任务是一次关键但能力有限的在轨验证，旨在为未来太空数据中心积累辐射、散热、供电和 AI 推理等方面的经验。
